articleTitle: Fractal based image coding scheme using Peano scan
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe an image compression system that incorporates Peano scan with a fractal-based coding scheme for intraframe compression and achieves high picture quality with a bit rate of <1 bit per pixel. An adaptive algorithm is included in the procedure in order to improve psycho-visual effects. A hardware implementation for this system with very low complexity is also proposed. This low-bit-rate, low-complexity, higher quality intraframe coding scheme can be used for transmitting high-resolution still images over an Integrated-Services Digital Network and is also suitable for many applications in which complexity is a major concern.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quantization error spectrum of sigma-delta modulators
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: It is shown that the spectra of the quantization noise of first- and second-order sigma-delta modulators contain strong peaks that depend on the amplitude of the input signal and are intolerable in many applications. This is contrary to the assumption that the quantizer noise from sigma-delta modulators is approximately white. An alternative modulator architecture comprising a cascade of first-order sigma-delta modulators is shown to have a white error spectrum. It is concluded that cascaded sigma-delta modulators exhibit a smooth noise spectrum and are thus suitable for direct replacement of Nyquist-rate PCM converters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An analytical method for optimal module orientation
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An important step in VLSI physical design is to determine the orientation of the modules after floorplanning. The authors describe an analytical method to determine the optimal module orientation in terms of estimated total wire length. The present formulation requires only the solution of set of linear equations to obtain a close approximation to the optimal solution. Thus, the computation speed is very high. Several variations of this method are also presented. The method was implemented and tested on a large number of examples. The results indicate that the method is very competitive in comparison with methods such as hill-climbing and simulated annealing in terms of the quality of the results and computation time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The LMS algorithm with momentum updating
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Several modifications of the well-known least-mean-square (LMS) algorithm have been proposed for improved operation. The authors analyze one such recent innovation that corresponds to the ordinary LMS algorithm with an additional momentum term, parameterized by the factor alpha . The analysis of convergence in the mean yields some novel behavior insofar that it leads to complex eigenvalues of the transition matrix for the mean weight vector. The convergence in the mean-square analysis demonstrates that instability will occur as alpha tends closer to 1, a result not predicted by the analysis of convergence in the mean.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CMOS circuit speed optimization based on switch level simulation
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a tool for transistor sizing for the purpose of speed optimization. The tool, called SLOP (switch-level optimization), is based on a switch-level simulation program for CMOS circuits. Consequently, the results are always verified by simulation. It gives the delay-area curve and the final sizes of each transistor according to the maximum width limitation specified by the user. Experimental results are presented. The typical improvement in circuit speed is 60%-90% with an area increase of 80%-110%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A systolic circuit for fast Hartley transform
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a systolic circuit for computing a fast algorithm performing the discrete Hartley transform (DHT). The proposed architecture employs a systolic elevator concept and CORDIC processors. The elevator assures local communications in the proposed algorithm, and the CORDIC processor makes it possible to enhance processing speed and exploit parallelism. The architecture appears to be regular and, therefore, very attractive for VLSI realizations. The computational cost necessary for computing the DFT (discrete Fourier transform) is also discussed with respect to other architectures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neural networks using analog multipliers
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A neural network implementation using MOSFET analog multipliers to construct weighted sums is described. This scheme permits asynchronous, analog operation of Hopfield style networks with fully programmable binary weights. This approach avoids the use of large-valued resistors which waste chip area or require special processing. Using this approach, analog neurons can be constructed in as few as 2+2 K transistors per Kb connection weight. An analytical model for the analog multipliers has been derived. This model has been used to stimulate a complete neural network for the traveling salesman problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A constrained two-dimensional adaptive digital filter with reduced computational complexity
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An adaptive 2-D digital filter is presented in which the filter is determined by a 1-D FIR (finite-impulse-response) prototype filter, and hence the computational complexity of the coefficient-update algorithm has an order of complexity that is similar to a 1-D adaptive filter. The convergence rate of the proposed structure is much faster than that of a direct-form 2-D LMS (least-mean-square) filter. Results of the hardware realization of the filter are presented that show its learning curve to be considerably less noisy than that of the 2-D direct-form LMS filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On frequency domain adaptive filters using the overlap-add method
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors introduce a frequency-domain adaptive filter (FDAF) configuration using the overlap-add method which has the same complexity and convergence behavior as the overlap-save configuration. It is shown that an FDAF using the overlap-add method can be realized with the same number of DFTs (discrete Fourier transforms) as the FDAF using the overlap-save method. The overlap-add implementation of an FDAF with seven DFTs is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A current mode algorithmic analog-to-digital converter
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel algorithmic analog-to-digital converter (ADC), using current instead of voltage to represent the signal, is described. The use of current eliminates switch-induced errors due to charge injection and results in reasonably high sampling rates without the need for large chip areas. To test this new concept, a 6-bit converter using a 3- mu m CMOS process was fabricated. The resulting circuit occupies a sampling rate of 200 kHz while drawing only 5 mW from a single 5-V supply. The speed of the ADC was limited by the settling time of the relatively large current mirrors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Switched-capacitor frequency-to-voltage and voltage-to-frequency converters based on charge-balancing principle
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Switched-capacitor frequency-to-voltage and voltage-to-frequency converters integrable onto a small chip area are developed. The conversion is insensitive to parasitic capacitances, capacitance ratio, offset voltages, and finite open-loop gains of op amps. Therefore, both converters allow accurate conversion over a wide dynamic range. The authors describe the circuit configurations, the principles of operation, and the experimental results obtained by breadboard converters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 3-connectivity augmentation problems
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors characterize a smallest 3-connectivity augmentation, involving the determination of a minimum set of edges to be added so as to 3-connect a given undirected simple graph. It is shown that there is an O( mod V mod ( mod V mod + mod E mod )/sup 2/) algorithm for finding a solution to the problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Theory and VLSI implementation of multilevel median filters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The properties of multilevel median filters are summarized, and a detailed analysis of their efficient implementation is given. In particular, a bit-serial compare/exchange module is described. This module is then used as the building block of a systolic array for the efficient implementation of these two-dimensional filtering algorithms. The architecture described yields a low area complexity, which allows a single chip VLSI implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fully parallel VLSI implementation of distributed arithmetic
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel architecture to implement distributed arithmetic in VLSI is presented. This architecture comprises a serial-in random-out multiport memory and a multi-input adder. The design of a 1.25- mu m CMOS convolution processor chip based on the architecture is reported. Issues in the development of chip architecture and design tools are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 2D FIR eigenfilters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel method for designing linear-phase two-dimensional (2D) FIR (finite impulse response) digital filters is presented. The method is based on minimizing an appropriately defined least-squares error function taken over the continuous passband and stopband frequency regions. The optimization problem reduces to that of computing the eigenvector corresponding to the minimum eigenvalue of a real symmetric and positive definite matrix. For symmetric fan filters, a closed-form solution is obtained that leads to a simple design procedure for this class of filters. The design method is general enough to incorporate both time- and frequency-domain constraints.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fast heuristics for optimal CMOS functional cell layout generation
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The problem of generating minimal-area CMOS functional cell layout can be converted to that of decomposing the transistor connection graph into a minimum number of subgraphs, each having a pair of Euler paths, with the same sequence of input labels on the N-graph and P-graph, which are portions of the graph corresponding to NMOS and PMOS parts, respectively. The authors propose a heuristic algorithm which yields a nearly minimum number of Euler paths from the path representation formulation which represents the given logic function. Subpath merging is done through a list processing scheme where the pairs of paths that results in the lowest cost are successively merged from all candidate merge pairs until no further path merging and no further reduction of the number of subgraphs are possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On switch-induced distortion in switched capacitor circuits
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Distortion in parasitic-insensitive switched-capacitor circuits is usually attributed to incomplete charging of capacitors due to finite switch on-resistance and nonlinear op-amp effects such as finite settling time. Even when these effects are made insignificant, unacceptable distortion may still result due to nonlinear charge injection during switch transitions. The authors present a preliminary analysis of this effect and, based on the analysis, ultraglow-distortion circuits are proposed and demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient multirate realization for narrow transition-band FIR filters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A filtering technique for reducing the computational complexity in FIR (finite-impulse-response) filters at any bandwidth is described. This technique uses a combination of multirate and complementary filters. It is shown that the resulting computational complexity is almost independent of the transition bandwidth of the filter, but depends somewhat on the cutoff frequency. It is concluded that any reasonable filter specification can be met by using about 45 multiplications per sample.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and application of a high quality three dimensional linear trajectory filter
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method is introduced for the design of 3D linear trajectory (LT) recursive digital filters which ideally have bowl-shaped passbands in the frequency domain. The passband approximation is obtained by adding the transfer functions of two 3D filters having elementary wedge-shaped passbands. The 3D elementary wedge filters are in turn obtained by applying a frequency-domain transformation to a highly selective 2D continuous-domain prototype fan filter. The design method is straightforward, computationally nonintensive, and leads to a guaranteed stable LT filter having a directional selectivity that is ideally independent of the spatial area occupied by the LT object. This advantage is demonstrated by means of a typical 3D LT filtering example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Primitive operator digital filter synthesis using a shift biased algorithm
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A graph-based synthesis technique has been developed which allows digital filters to be realized with significantly reduced numbers of primitive arithmetic operations. Previously presented work has relied on the use of unity-gain graph edges. These methods are extended by the authors to permit the inclusion of edges with gains which may assume any power of two. This facilitates a tradeoff between addition or subtraction and shift operations which can be beneficial in many implementations. For VLSI implementations especially, judicious placement of processing elements, routing, and allocation of pipeline registers, make for an efficient filter implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 30 MHz programmable CMOS video FIR filter and correlator
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A VLSI chip has been designed to perform two important functions in video image processing, namely, programmable finite-impulse response (FIR) filtering and correlation. In the FIR mode, the chip performs eight states (taps) of filtering with 9 b of video data and 8 b of coefficients. The coefficients can be dynamically changed by loading in a new set. The chips can be directly cascaded to extend the stages of filtering in multiples of eight, without any additional glue chips. In the correlation mode, the chip correlates the input signals. The chip has 32200 transistors and has been fabricated in 2- mu m, double-metal low-power silicon CMOS technology. Testing indicated that the chip worked at 31 MHz at room temperature and 5 V.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CMOS ASIC devices for the measurement of short time intervals
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Two time-to-digital converters are designed, with special emphasis on searching for and modeling the causes of timing jitter in CMOS devices. The time base is formed by an external high-frequency three-phase clock in the first design and by tapped on-chip delay-lines in the second circuit. The single-shot resolutions of the circuits are about 7 and 0.5 ns.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An algorithm for one-sided 1/sub 1/ optimization with application to circuit design centering
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A highly efficient algorithm for one-sided nonlinear 1/sub 1/ optimization combines a trust region Gauss-Newton method and a quasi-Newton method. The proposed method is used as an integral part of an approach to design centering and yield enhancement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A ratio-independent cyclic A/D conversion technique
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A cyclic A/D (analog-to-digital) conversion technique is presented for achieving a conversion performance independent of capacitor ratios. Based on the concept of charge redistribution, the method requires only two operations per bit. This technique can be realized by a switched-capacitor circuit with two balanced operation amplifiers and a comparator. With the balanced structure, the charge injection effect of the switches is also effectively minimized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On H/sub infinity / filtering in multivariable discrete-time systems
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A solution for the discrete-time multivariable H/sub infinity / filtering problem is presented. The relationship between the least-squares filtering and H/sub infinity / filtering design methods is considered, and the H/sub infinity / filtering solution is obtained by embedding the problem within the least-squares filtering solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Decision trees applied to on-line transient stability assessment of power systems
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Decision rules provided by an inductive inference method are examined for online use in transient stability analysis and preventive control. Consideration is given first to the stability region, expressed in terms of the relevant static, prefault parameters of the system, automatically identified by the decision rules. Stability margins are then proposed, measuring the distance to instability, i.e. the degree of the system robustness in facing a major disturbance. Methods to act on these margins in order to reinforce stability, if necessary, are further suggested. The stability measures and their use are illustrated using simulation results obtained on the basis of a realistic example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sensitivity based testing of nonlinear circuits
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a sensitivity-based method to test nonlinear circuits with small variations of element parameters. Several excitation levels and signal frequencies are used to improve system testability. This method is illustrated using piecewise-linear models, although it can be generalized to handle other nonlinear characteristics. The QR algorithm is used to select test points and ensure numerical stability. In the case of a sufficient number of measurement points, a linear, fault verification technique can also be used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital bilinear LDI ladder filters using lattice equivalents and wave concepts
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Lossless discrete integrator (LDI)-based digital filters which implement bilinear transformed third- and sixth-order elliptic transfer functions are presented. The filters are designed by converting ladder prototypes to lattice prototypes, and realizing the resulting lattice impedance reflectances with LDI elements. The structures which result are amenable to compact biserial implementation and require only as many multiplication operations as the filter order. It is concluded that the lattice bilinear LDI formulation may be applicable to the design of parasitic insensitive switched-capacitor filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An edge-oriented compaction scheme based on multiple storage quad tree
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: As the complexity of integrated circuit design increases, the need for a computer-aided layout editing tool becomes critical. However, the most critical role in a VLSI CAD layout tool is known as the compactor. The authors describe an efficient edge-oriented, error-tolerance and mixed-constraint graph compactor based on a simple and fast region-query data structure-the multiple storage (MS) quad tree. The MS quad tree data structure supports a dexterous region search and inherently can be used to handle extended objects such as rhomboids and polygons.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transfer functions for nonlinear systems via Fourier-Borel transforms
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: It is demonstrated that the general response of nonlinear dynamical systems can be expressed in terms of their transfer functions in an analogous way to the linear systems. The transfer functions are defined as the generalized series for the response of the nonlinear dynamical system which is initially at rest and which is loaded by a unit step function. These transfer functions are obtainable through symbolic computer algebra.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the geometry of 2D systems
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors propose a geometric theory for 2-D systems, based on suitable notions of controlled invariance and conditional invariance. In addition to specific results on disturbance decoupling, model matching and output controllability problems, this approach provides a better insight into the structural properties of a 2-D system. Namely, it makes it possible to introduce a set of invariants and a dynamics which, in the 2-D framework, play the role of the zeros at infinity and of the zero-dynamics of the classical linear systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A canonical continuous-time MOSFET-capacitor filter with high linearity
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors propose a synthesis of fully integrated canonical continuous-time filters with a high degree of linearity. The synthesis method is based on a differential current-integrator with a simple capacitor. A method to reduce the number of MOS transistors has also been presented. A third-order leapfrog filter is realized by the proposed method as an example. A total harmonic distortion less than 0.03% is obtained by SPICE analysis. The proposed method is advantageous, especially in the realization of higher-order filters, because of the reduction of higher-order filters, because of the reduction in chip area and manufacturing cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Novel method for realizing higher-order immittance function using current conveyors
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel method for realizing a higher-order immittance function using current conveyors (CCs) is proposed. By introducing the nullator-norator technique, many simulation circuits can be systematically derived. The derived circuits have the following advantages: (1) simplicity for circuit design for immittance function simulation; (2) applicability for the higher-order immittance function simulation using additional CCs; and (3) low active sensitivities of realized immittance functions. The higher-order immittance function can be applied to various filters. As examples of its applications, high-pass and low-pass filters are given with experimental results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis and evaluation of expert's knowledge for power system restoration by mathematical programming method
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors compare numerical and knowledge methods through the analysis and evaluation of an expert's knowledge in solving a network restoration problem. Analysis and evaluation are performed in a way that compares the solutions to network restoration problems given by numerical and knowledge methods. It is shown that knowledge methods can lead to an optimal solution efficiently in almost all cases and are effective in obtaining a feasible solution for complex problems. To take further advantage of the knowledge, it is proposed that the knowledge method is integrated with the numerical one as its pre- or post-processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 2-D interpolation, matrix factorization and applications to signal processing
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method for solving a class of 2-D interpolation problems is presented. The method is not restricted to uniform interpolation points and has the attractive features of recursive computability and permanence of the solution. By combining two different approaches to the problem, the authors obtained the LU decomposition of the interpolation matrix without having to check the nonsingularity of submatrices. This decomposition gives the computational advantage of reducing the original problem to the solution of two triangular systems. The method can be used for the design of 1-D and 2-D FIR (finite-impulse response) filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Concepts for the restitution of video signals using MOS analog circuits
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Two architectures of a video decoder using an analog 2- mu m CMOS process are examined. One includes digital oversampling filters, while the other one is based on switched-capacitor (SC) filters. The first architecture has been fabricated and led to a 38-mm/sup 2/ circuit including more than 40000 transistors. An estimation of the SC solution makes it possible to obtain a chip of about 10 mm/sup 2/ and less than 10000 transistors. The power consumption is nearly identical for both solutions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A CMOS implementation of a video-rate successive approximation A/D converter
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Previous approaches to video-rate CMOS A/D (analog-to-digital) converters are based on fully-parallel, subrange, or pipeline architectures. The authors describe a 5-MHz 8-bit experimental design of a successive-approximation A/D converter using 3- mu m CMOS technology. Since neither capacitors nor a resistor string are needed in the current-switching technique, a conventional digital technology can be used. The use of the CMOS current-switch technique makes bipolar input signals possible. A circuit realization of a high-speed successive approximation register is also presented, using a single phase clock. The proposed technique is compatible with digital VLSI technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On dual Eulerian paths and circuits in plane graphs
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Given a nonseparable plane graph G, a path or circuit is called dual if it is also a path or circuit, respectively, in the geometric dual of G. Motivated by a layout design problem of CMOS integrated circuits, the authors consider some problems of partitioning the edges of G into the minimum number of dual paths or circuits. The results include a constructive proof of the fact that the following problems are solvable in polynomial time: determining whether G has a dual circuit; finding a dual Eulerian path or circuit if one exists; and finding the minimum set of dual paths that partitions the edges of G when G has no dual circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new digital-to-analog conversion algorithm
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An algorithm is described which starts digital-to-analog conversion with the most significant bit. This algorithm can be realized by using only sample/hold circuits, and thus permits high-speed conversion. Error analysis shows that a conversion accuracy of 10 bits or higher is easily obtainable with a monolithic implementation. The architecture of data converters using this algorithm and some experimental results are also given to confirm the principles of operation. it is concluded that the proposed algorithm is universal in that it is applicable to cyclic, successive-approximation, sequential-flash, pipeline, and flash conversion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A DSP architecture for 64 kbps motion video codec
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe an architectural study of a digital signal processor (DSP) well suited for video codec. This DSP consists of specified resources optimized for video signal processing, such as the instruction set, buses, data memories, execution unit, address generators, sequencer, and DMAC. The performance of the DSP is evaluated through several video coding sequences. The architecture of a multiprocessor configuration for video codec, which will allow flexible algorithm and variable picture format, is also examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Convergence of waveform relaxation method
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Work on establishing a framework for discussing the convergence of waveform-relaxation-type processes is surveyed. Methods for accelerating the iteration are examined, with the discussion limited to the linear autonomous problem. Consideration is given to continuous iteration, discretized iteration, finite windows, and differential/algebraic equation systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Circuit simulation on a hypercube
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a concurrent circuit simulation program, CONCISE. The simulator has been implemented in a purely message-passing environment and runs on the Intel iPSC as well as on the Sequent Balance, Sun 3:s, and VAXen. CONCISE uses waveform relaxation to decouple the transient analysis simulation into subtasks. Robustness has been improved by using a novel window-splitting scheme. The sequential fraction varies between 2 and 0.1% when run on an Intel iPSC, which implies that 50-1000 processors can be used efficiently. It is concluded that a granularity as low as one circuit-node per node can be used. Speedup is increased for each node that is added even though overhead due to load imbalance and message overhead increases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transient analysis of a class of mixed lumped and distributed constant circuits
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An approach to the transient analysis of a class of linear and time-invariant lumped constant circuits cascaded by dispersionless transmission lines is presented. The transmission lines are numerically analyzed by the modified central difference method, and the lumped constant circuits are analyzed by the state variable approach to meet the boundary conditions. Simulation results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Passive symmetrical RLC filters suitable for active simulation
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A filter synthesis procedure is presented which generates physically symmetrical or asymmetrical passive structures even for approximations having simple transmission zeros. The procedure is based on the unbalancing of a symmetrical lattice realization. The obtained networks are interesting as prototypes for fully integrated active simulation, due to the symmetrical layouts, and to the naturally gradient-insensitive structure made possible by the symmetry of sensitivities in the filter structure. Fifth- and fourth-order normalized elliptic lowpass filters are considered as examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Routh type approximation for discrete system
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method of reduction for a discrete system is presented. The denominator of the reduced model is directly obtained in z-domain from the denominator of the higher-order system. The denominator of the reduced model is directly obtained from a Routh-type table. The numerator of the reduced model is obtained either by matching the discrete time moments or by minimizing the step response error constructed in discrete time domain and computed in z-domain. The stability of the reduced model is guaranteed if the higher-order system is stable. A numerical example is examined which involves the determination of a second-order reduced model for a fourth-order digital filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Diagnosability of analog circuits-a graph theoretical approach
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Necessary and almost sufficient topological conditions for both node and branch fault diagnosis are presented and analyzed. The representation of the network through a pair of graphs constitutes the theoretical basis of the proposed conditions. These conditions are applicable to both active and passive networks. Examples are given to show the application of the proposed topological condition in fault diagnosis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New s-z transformation and its switched capacitor realization
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A novel s-z transformation called the mixed-discrete integrator, (MDI), which results in less frequency warping than the conventional transformations, is proposed. It is derived by combining the bilinear and lossless-discrete-integrator transformations with ratio k(0<or=k<or=1). The realization of switched-capacitor filters using this transformation is discussed for a leapfrog structure.<<ETX>>

articleTitle: GaAs IC technology, circuits, and systems
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Current commercial GaAs IC technology is reviewed along with IC yield and reliability. Standard digital products and standard-cell ASICs, (application-specific integrated circuits) are described. CRAY-3 GaAs implementation is discussed as a system application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An application of chaos: generating binary pseudo-random sequences
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present an important application of chaos: generating binary pseudorandom sequences (BPRSs). A method for extracting a class of BPRSs from chaos is proposed. The randomness of such BPRSs is proved. The results show that the BPRSs have the same randomness as white noise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Perfect reconstruction QMF structures which yield linear phase FIR analysis filters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a perfect reconstruction FIR (finite-impulse response) linear-phase lattice structure for the two-channel quadrature-mirror-filter (QMF) bank. This structure covers most pairs of perfect reconstruction FIR linear-phase analysis filters which have the same (odd) order. For general number of channels M, conditions are derived which any QMF perfect reconstruction linear phase structure must obey. A design example is presented for the M=2 case.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Alias cancellation and distortion elimination in multi-dimensional QMF banks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A necessary and sufficient condition is derived for alias cancellation in two-dimensional (2-D) quadrature-mirror-filter (QMF) banks. It requires the product of the polyphase matrices associated with the analysis and synthesis banks to be 2-D pseudocirculant. The conditions for eliminating phase or magnitude distortion are derived. A method for obtaining perfect reconstruction is suggested. The pseudocirculant property also arises in 2-D block filtering. The results can be generalized to higher dimensions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A scalable synchronous system
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The performance of the synchronous timing scheme for VLSI-based systems is examined. It is shown that traditional clocking used in this scheme leads to serious performance shortcoming, particularly for submicrometer technologies. A novel mode of clocking is proposed and examined in detail. This clocking mode makes the performance of the synchronous system almost scalable with scaling the feature size of MOS devices. The application of this mode of clocking to H-tree networks, usually used in systolic arrays, is also investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FIR transfer functions with arbitrary amplitude and phase, with application to the design of quasi-all-pass delay equalizers
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel technique is presented for the design of FIR (finite-impulse-response) digital filters with simultaneous conditions on the amplitude and phase responses. The technique can be used to design any type of FIR filter, but is particularly useful for the design of quasi-all-pass phase equalizers. The method is based on a polynomial termed the arbitrary phase and amplitude polynomial. The technique was illustrated by equalizing the delay of an elliptic IIR (infinite-impulse-response) filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The master-slave IIR filter adaptation algorithm
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An adaptive IIR (infinite-impulse response) filtering algorithm is proposed which combines advantages of two error criteria. The algorithm is termed master-slave, as an auxiliary adaptive filter (the slave) is used to assist the adaptation of the main adaptive IIR filter. By using an additional FIR (finite-impulse-response) filter to minimize the output error criterion, an IIR filter can be adapted using the preferred equation error criterion, while noise present in the desired filter response will not lead to biased parameter values. This enables IIR filters to converge much more rapidly than is possible with output error minimization alone. A steepest-descent form of the algorithm has been derived which uses a simple test to guarantee stability of the adaptive filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Equalisation of analogue to digital converter nonlinearities
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A signal-processing technique called threshold tracking is presented which can improve the linearity of any analog-to-digital conversion circuit (ADC). The basic idea is to use a mapping of the original output codes and their associated nonideal quantization levels to a set of codes whose corresponding quantization levels more closely match those of an ideal ADC. When the mapped codes are then assumed to be associated with ideal quantization levels by the rest of the signal processing system, the error between the actual and the ideal levels is reduced. The equalization system is described and the convergence and equalization performance in the presence of training signal noise is shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A digital frequency synthesizer with a phase accumulator
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Describes a digital frequency synthesizer that uses a novel phase-estimation technique in which a phase accumulator is used as a reference generator and the phase error is treated as a numerical value. The performance of the proposed system is verified by both experiments and theoretical analysis. It is shown that the proposed system has faster frequency switching speed and better synchronous mode than the conventional PLL system because of the characteristics of the phase-frequency detector and the high-frequency reference.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High frequency switched capacitor filters for CMOS technology
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors consider with the development of high-frequency switched-capacitor filters for implementation using CMOS technology. The development is focussed on the use of an amplifier with complementary (nondifferential) inputs in which the DC voltage levels at the two inputs and at the output are all substantially different, and which is thought to allow the closest approach to the maximum theoretical switching frequency for the technology. In the resulting circuits, the conventional boundaries between the amplifier and the remainder of the SC circuit become less distinct and the integrator has to be treated as the basic unit. Filter examples are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis of optimal discrete pulse modulation waveforms through an integer quadratic program
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors introduce a physically based objective function for determining optimal discrete pulse modulation waveforms in power electronics applications. Using this objective function, it is demonstrated that the problem of selecting an optimal waveform reduces to a quadratic zero-one integer program. It is shown that the structure of this zero-one program lends itself to a bounding algorithm that allows many of the branches in the search tree to be eliminated, considerably reducing the computational cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of complex coefficient FIR digital filters using weighted approximation
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Two theorems related to the Fourier transform of the complex time function are shown. By using these theorems and the Remes exchange algorithm, a minimax design method for complex-coefficient FIR (finite-impulse response) digital filters is proposed. The method reduces the complexity of the calculations, because the real and imaginary parts of the desired impulse response can be designed independently. It has been shown that this method attains sufficient accuracy in approximation both magnitude and phase (group delay) responses by design examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault location of linear nonreciprocal circuit with tolerance
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Based on probability theory, a method for the fault diagnosis of linear nonreciprocal circuits with tolerance is proposed. This method can locate multiple faults in the circuit into a certain branch set. The element-separating-bound concept is introduced for diagnosing single faults; using this approach, a single fault may be located further into a smaller branch set or even determined uniquely.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive-length median filters for image processing
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors propose algorithms using adaptive-length median filters, for improving impulse-noise-removal performance for image processing. The algorithms can achieve significantly better image quality than regular (fixed-length) median filters when the images are corrupted by impulse noise. One of the advantages of the algorithms is that, when realized in hardware, the additional circuitry required is rather simple. Furthermore, the algorithms can easily be integrated into efficient hardware realizations for median filters. Performance-simulation results and implementation issues are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A differential input/output integrator without p-n-p transistors and its application to leapfrog filter synthesis
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors propose a differential input/output integrator to implement monolithic video-frequency analog filters. The proposed integrator requires no p-n-p transistors and works with a single 5-V supply. The proposed integrator was implemented by a 3- mu m bipolar process and a third-order video-frequency filter was built on the basis of the integrators. A leapfrog filter synthesis method fully utilizing the differential input/output integrators is described. The obtained filter has a low sensitivity to time constants of the integrators in the passband. Experimental results confirm the testability of the integrator and the filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel implementation of a median filtering algorithm
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A synchronous parallel implementation of a two-dimensional median filtering algorithm is presented. Through this implementation, the effectiveness of a novel data partitioning scheme that balances the work-load distribution among the different processors of a multiprocessor system is demonstrated. The proposed data partitioning scheme has reduced the idling time of the processors at synchronization points for algorithms that depend on data characteristics which, as in typical images, could differ considerably from region to region.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assessing security assessment
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors discuss aspect-operator-test graphs, a method for representing and evaluating engineering tasks, and apply them to power system security assessment. The result indicates where research is most needed. An analysis of existing practices for short-term security assessment shows that their greatest weakness is their complete lack of clearly articulated, readily applicable, quality assurance tests. Second in the list of deficiencies is the variation of aspect population densities over the security assessment task. Last on the list are the algorithmic screening procedures used by many short-term assessment schemes to produce a worst-case list of contingencies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ISDN echo cancellation circuit (IEC), a transceiver for the subscriber loop
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The digital part of a two-chip U-interface transceiver for the subscriber loop is presented. According to the ISDN (integrated-services digital network) standard all communication control and algorithmic requirements are implemented for a 144-kb/s full duplex data transmission. The chip is implemented in a double-metal 2- mu m CMOS technology with an area of 8.2 mm*7.3 mm containing 58000 transistors, 15000 of which are implemented in a cell approach, the rest in hand-tuned digital signal processor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two robust Remez methods for the design of FIR digital filters meeting prescribed specifications
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Two methods (the maximum ripple method and the extra-ripple method) for designing optimal Chebyshev multiband FIR (finite-impulse response) digital filters are introduced. These methods usually converge rapidly even when the number of bands is large, and with the addition of some simple heuristic techniques will produce filters which are free of transition-region magnitude-response anomalies. Both of these methods use a Remez-type exchange algorithm, a novel initialization strategy, and a selective search which reduces the amount of computation needed to carry out a design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A procedure for efficient FIR filter design using prefilters
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Digital FIR (finite-impulse response) prefilter structures with periodic impulse response are introduced. By appropriately cascading these prefilters, large stopband attenuation can be obtained, relieving the task of the equalizer. A systematic design procedure for the cascade of prefilters and the equalizer is given, leading to computationally efficient FIR filters. Design examples are included, demonstrating that the proposed design procedure leads to significant savings in the number of arithmetic operations as compared to recent proposed designs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Switched-capacitor digital-analogue converters with built-in FIR filtering
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Summary form only given. The traditional solutions for the conversion of digital signals into the continuous-time domain include a digital-to-analog converter (DAC) followed by a reconstruction filter. Since ordinary DACs only provide a very low selectivity filtering action due to the particular sampling format of the output signal, the reconstruction filter alone is responsible for the shaping of the output imaging spectrum. The authors propose a type of DAC which incorporates an FIR (finite-impulse-response) transfer function, and which can, therefore, allow a considerable reduction of the selectivity requirements of the reconstruction filter, or even their elimination. These devices, realized using switched-capacitor techniques, are attractive for integrated circuit fabrication, and their good performance is demonstrated by means of a simple discrete component model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of the applicability of the network flow approach to the emergency service restoration problem
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The graph theory/network flow approach to the emergency-service restoration problem is discussed. The mixer integer programming formulation looks rigorous and concise. However, its usefulness appears to be very limited due to computational difficulties. By introducing artificial branches and a source and sink, the problem may be formulated as a maximal-flow problem in a restricted sense. In this case, zero-one decision variables representing switch status should be handled separately after the solution to the completely connected network is obtained. It is shown that the straight-forward application of the graph theory/network flow approach is not suitable for the problem. This simply points out difficulties associated with the problem and also suggests that heuristic algorithms need to be used to handle problems of this nature.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stable nonlinear recursive filters for edge enhancing noise smoothing of images
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Stability conditions for nonlinear recursive filters of the form y(n)=f(x(n, y(n-1)), y(n-2), . . ., y(n-N)) where f is equal to a linear combination of x(n), y(n-i), i=1, 2, . . ., N with nonconstant coefficients. A specific scheme is proposed for simultaneous noise smoothing and edge sharpening of images. The problem of distortion similar to that due to the nonlinear phase of linear recursive filters is solved by incorporating multidirectional filtering methods. Results of using this nonlinear recursive image filter show that the quality of image is not only restored but also improved in the case of low- to medium-variance noise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A switching circuit scheme for a satellite site diversity system
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Problems connected with a satellite site diversity system (SDS) i.e., diversity synchronization, diversity switching control, and interconnection of two diversity antenna sites are discussed, and different solutions are considered. A preliminary baseline for the SDS includes circuit solutions for the alignment and switching equipment using elastic memories, the choice of beacon signal attenuation as a quality parameter, and the adoption of an error-free optical-fiber link between the two diversity stations. As an example, the implementation of the SDS relative to the experimental Olympus satellite is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple method for all solutions of a piecewise linear network
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An efficient algorithm is proposed for searching for all solutions of a piecewise-linear resistive network. Let P/sub n/ be the number of largest segments of PWL resistors, and P/sub n-1/ the second largest. Then, the algorithm presented is better than the brute-force method by a factor of P/sub n/*P/sub n-1/ and the Chua and Ying (1982) method, the most efficient method at the present time, by a factor of at least P/sub n-1/. The algorithm is based on a novel theorem for piecewise-linear networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A voice pattern matching LSI based on a new speaker-independent continuous voice recognition scheme
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A novel CMOS special-purpose LSI, the MSM6851, is described which realizes a voice-pattern-matching scheme for speaker-independent continuous voice recognition. A voice signal was specified by a specific pattern drawn on a plane with two axes: time axis and frequency axis. A simultaneous matching procedure on two axes was realized by a vector-processing LSI to absorb the difference of voice uttered by individual speakers. The vector-processing architecture was found to be essential for realizing the high-speed processing required by the proposed algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Direct form revisited: recursive filter implementation using higher-order direct form sections
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The cascade implementation of recursive digital filters using fourth-order direct form sections is investigated. The implementation with TMS320 processors is studied in detail. The finite-wordlength performance and the implementation costs of six different test filters are compared. It is concluded that the cascade of fourth-order direct form sections with second-order error feedback provides a very effective and low-noise structure for signal processor implementation, except with very narrowband filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The analytic theory of semiuniform lossy broadband matching networks
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: D.C. Youla's (see IEEE Trans. Circuit Theory, vol.CT-11, p.30-50, 1964) broadband matching theory for lossless networks is developed systematically for the semiuniform lossy networks which are used in MICs and MMICs (monolithic microwave integrated circuits). The unitary property of the scattering matrix of semiuniform lossy two-port has been proved. The constraints of load-transmission zeros on the semiuniform lossy broadband matching networks can be designed using the proposed method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementing signal processing functions on ternary encoded delta-modulated pulse streams
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors investigate the possibility of processing analog signals directly in delta-modulated pulse stream format. They demonstrate a class of linear operations on data represented as a ternary delta-modulated pulse stream (X/sub n/) corresponding to the analog quantity x(t). These functions make it possible to implement a set of DSP (digital signal processing) algorithms directly on the delta-modulator output data. A method for ternary delta multiplier synthesis is presented and illustrated by a DM filter example. It is concluded that the proposed multiplier can conveniently implement a FIR (finite impulse response) filter structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two-dimensional polyphase filter banks with arbitrary number of subband channels
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Two-dimensional (2-D) polyphase filter banks for 2-D subband signal processing systems are described. New 2-D polyphase filter banks with an arbitrary number of subband channels are presented. The concept of nonsymmetric frequency band allocation for the construction of subband bandpass filters is extended to the 2-D case. The subband bandpass filters required in both analysis and synthesis filter banks are then constructed from the frequency translations of a 2-D prototype lowpass filter. The constraints of perfect aliasing cancellation and signal reconstruction are derived for cases of separable and nonseparable 2-D prototype lowpass filters. Simulation results that confirm the theoretical analyses are also provided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An evolutionary VLSI chip set for ISDN
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe a cost-effective and flexible approach to introducing the ISDN (integrated-services digital network) into System 12 with respect to CMOS and nMOS integrated circuits. The chip set includes three transmission devices for basic or primary rate access: a two-wire U-interface transceiver using the 4B3T line code, a four-wire transceiver and the PRA trunk logical interface. The layer 2 function is covered by a device including functions for link layer protocols on the D-channel or on the B-channel for both LAPD and CCITT No.7 signaling schemes. An on board controller interface provides the control and transmission interface between the line modules and the switching network. The set is completed with a multistandard rate adapter for terminal adapter application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ripple and transition-width trade-off in the design of elliptic filters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In the design of elliptic function filters, passband and stopband specifications are used to determine the order of the filter. In standard design methods, the calculated order is a fraction and the actual filter is designed by using an order which is the smallest integer greater than the calculated fraction. The authors shown how one can use this effective increase to further reduce either the passband ripple, the stopband ripple, or the transition bandwidth to give a well-defined optimal approximation. It is shown how to start with the order and design an optimal elliptic function filter by minimizing any one of the other approximation measures. The authors posed four optimal filter design problems using the Chebyshev error criterion in the passband and stopband. An algorithm is described that allows the solution of these problems using Jacobian elliptic function theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fast hopping frequency synthesizer for agile radar
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe a direct synthesizer that combines direct analog and digital techniques to produce a low-noise fast switching X-band source. Direct digital frequency synthesis performance in terms of spurious content is described. The RF and microwave frequency synthesizers are described, and the switching-speed and phase-noise performance are characterized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Acoustic noise cancellation in a multiple noise source environment
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A multireference adaptive noise canceller (MRANC) is derived from an analysis of a multiple-noise-source acoustic environment. The approach places a microphone near each noise source and one microphone near the speech source. Each noise reference microphone receives a signal primarily from its associated noise source along with contributions from other sources. This is called coupling, which degrades the MRANC performance under certain circumstances. The optimal noise cancelling structure is determined. From this optimal filter structure, several filter structures for processing the reference signals are derived based on assumptions about the environment. Quantitative test results from real-life environments are presented and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On an order of reviving inaccessible nodes eliminated with the repeated use of a generalized star to polygon transformation
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The restorability problem for an LCR network involves the reviving (one by one) of inaccessible nodes eliminated by the repeated use of a generalized star-to-polygon transformation. A complete solution to a graph-theoretic problem that has been posed in relation to the restorability problem is presented. A novel problem in connection with a generalization of this graph-theoretic problem is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis and calibration of large analog circuits
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method to test and calibrate linear circuits is proposed. A tested circuit is partitioned at nodes where the voltage measurements are taken. Test equations are formulated on the basis of Kirchoff's current law equations at the partition points. This results in the Jacobian matrix with a sparse block structure. The test points selection and the element evaluation can be performed in parallel, reducing computation time and enhancing the test performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An optimal cardinality-constrained territory map on a network
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors consider the problem of finding an optimal cardinality-constrained territory map, and propose an algorithm for the problem with the time and space complexities of O(n(m+k log k)) and O(n+m), respectively, where k,n, and m are the numbers of centers, vertices, and edges of a given network. It is noted that maps of this sort can be applied to an assignment problem, e.g., the problem of assigning an employer (vertex) to a project leader (center).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scheduling jobs on a tree-connected processor system
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A tree-connected processor system (TPS) is one where m (>or=1) processors are connected to constitute a rooted tree. The authors study the problem of finding a feasible schedule for a TPS for n jobs with release times and deadlines. It is shown that the problem can be solved in O(mn log n) time if jobs have unit processing times.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Switched-capacitor realization of a Walsh transform circuit and its application to sequency filtering
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A novel switched-capacitor discrete Walsh transform circuit is proposed. The Walsh hardware transformation is improved in simplicity by using the proposed circuit, and this circuit has a speed advantage because of analog processing. Furthermore, a switched-capacitor inverse Walsh transform circuit is constructed. A switched-capacitor sequence filter is also proposed which combines the Walsh transform circuit and its inverse.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient high speed delayed multipath two-dimensional recursive digital filter architecture
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An efficient transformation method for the realization of a delayed multipath two-dimensional IIR (infinite impulse response) digital filter is presented. Although the structure does not give 100% multiprocessing efficiency, the maximum overall throughput improvement that can be achieved is high. The delayed multipath structure has been successfully applied to the realization of an FIR (finite impulse response) digital filter. In actual implementation, the method involves difficulty when applied directly to an IIR digital filter because of the inherent timing constraint in the recursive loop. With the transformation method, extra loop delay is allowed in the recursive part of the multipath structure. Consequently, the problem of inherent timing constraint in the recursive loop is solved. Furthermore, the transformation method is efficient in terms of computational complexity, throughput improvement, and multiprocessing efficiency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simultaneous amplitude and phase approximation for lumped and IIR-filters
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An efficient method is described for simultaneous amplitude and phase approximation of low-pass and bandpass filters. The two kinds of approximation are based on linear interpolation techniques and are carried out alternatively. When approximating digital (infinite-impulse-response) IIR filters, the phase distortion caused by the bilinear transformation is taken into consideration. The efficiency of the method is illustrated by the approximation of a seventh-order low-pass filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of tap-changer dynamics and construction of voltage stability regions
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The destabilizing behavior of on-load tap-changers is an important mechanism responsible for the voltage collapse of power systems. The authors use a nonlinear dynamic model of the tap-changer, impedance loads, and decoupled reactive power-voltage relations to reconstruct the collapse. Based on the proposed M-bus network model, results presented include (1) a criterion for voltage stability, (2) a method to obtain a voltage region, and (3) qualitative characterizations of the equilibria.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Minimum length linear transistor arrays in MOS
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The following abstract problem is solved: given a two-terminal series-parallel (sp) graph, find an sp-equivalent graph in which the number of vertices with odd degree is minimum, where an sp-equivalence class consists of the graphs with the same series and parallel connections except for their order. The motivation for this problem is to find a minimum-length one-dimensional transistor array for MOS-discharge networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach to analog fault diagnosis and an experimental diagnostic system
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An approach to analog fault diagnosis for resistive circuits is presented. The diagnosis equations derived on the basis of nodal-voltage measurement are quadratic. Using the concept of DC equivalent resistance, the authors propose an efficient approach to the diagnosis of nonlinear resistive circuits. Based on this approach, they have implemented an experimental analog automatic diagnostic system, which can diagnose any fault elements in practical linear resistive circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Resistive circuits with several solutions
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Necessary and sufficient conditions are given under which a resistive circuit may have several, but finitely many solutions. Whether it actually has several solutions depends on the values of the sources and linear resistors as well as on the characteristics of the nonlinear resistors. Such circuits are required for static memory applications of all kinds, including associative memories realized by neural networks. These criteria are given in terms of linear circuits and circuit topology. In addition, the minimal memory circuits are characterized. They constitute the building blocks for more complicated memory circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of SC MOS delta and delta-sigma modulators to nonlinear signal processing
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors investigate and discuss the applicability of CMOS switched-capacitor (SC) delta-sigma modulators to the design of basic nonlinear devices and circuits such as multiplier-dividers, generalized integrators, correlators, and piecewise-linear function generators. Different structures for the realization of such devices are proposed and their performance is demonstrated by computer simulations. The performance of precision and robust analog multipliers is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Complex modelling of real system based on positive frequency range
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: It is shown that, using the system identification procedure, a real system can be represented approximately by a complex model with half-reduced order. The model is estimated by the least-squares method extended to the complex case. The model is found to be quite insensitive to coefficient perturbations. Complex digital filtering is considered as an application of the proposed model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A singular system realization for arbitrary matrix fraction descriptions
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A realization algorithm is presented which determines a singular system realization from an arbitrary right matrix fraction description (MFD). Neither the properness nor the column-reducedness of the right MFD is required. The realization also possesses some important properties which, although in a generalized sense, are similar to those of Wolovich's realization (1972).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A digital single sideband modulator
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe an interpolation method which greatly simplifies the RF complexity of D.K. Weaver's (1956) method of single-sideband (SSB) generation for a digital implementation. The baseband I and Q signal samples are interpolated using simple accumulators and the interpolated samples are multiplexed to produce the SSB signal samples. The proposed method would be ideally suited for generating SSB at a fixed intermediate frequency, and is also suitable for generating SSB by selecting one of the harmonics of the carrier frequency using a simple filter. Simulations confirm that good performance can be achieved with this method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Location of faulty subnetworks in analog network
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
