abstract: A compute-node-current-sum procedure is proposed for the diagnosis of faulty subnetworks. The sensitivity of this procedure enables preestimation whether or not the test points are reasonable. To simplify the postfault computation, the equivalent nominal model of linear subnetwork is used. Finally, linear active network and op-amp examples are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Roundoff noise generated by orthogonal building blocks in signal processing structures
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The statistics of roundoff errors produced by the multiplication of a random input vector with an orthogonal matrix can be expressed in terms of the characteristic function of the input vector. The case of a 2*2 orthogonal matrix is analyzed by assuming that the input probability mass function follows a jointly Gaussian envelope. It is found that for small dynamic ranges the two errors are not necessarily uncorrelated. However, they are uncorrelated for large dynamic range. The lossless FIR (finite-impulse-response) lattice with quantizers is considered as an example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A codimension-3 bifurcation problem and its application to electrical circuits
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A bifurcation phenomenon which arises from the interaction of static and dynamic modes in the vicinity of a compound critical point of a nonlinear autonomous system is considered. The critical point is characterized by a double zero and a pair of pure imaginary eigenvalues of the Jacobian. A set of simplified differential equations is obtained by applying the unification technique coupled with the intrinsic harmonic balancing procedure. Based on the simplified equations, the equilibrium solutions, Hopf bifurcation solutions and quasiperiodic motions lying on 2-D tori, as well as the associated stability conditions, are explored. An example drawn from electrical circuits is analyzed to demonstrate the direct applicability of the analytic results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive noise cancelling by accelerated gradients techniques
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Demonstrates the application of the method of steepest descent with exact linear search (SDELS) and the conjugate gradients method (CGM) to adaptive noise cancelling (ANC). An adaptive algorithm based on the method of SEDLS is proposed and its computational complexity and numerical stability are discussed. The performance of the algorithms in terms of convergence speed, tracking data nonstationarities, and the effect of fixed-point roundoff errors is illustrated by simulating a single channel ANC scheme using the standard recursive least-squares algorithm and the proposed algorithm. These results illustrate the close performance of both algorithms and verify the lower numerical sensitivity of the proposed algorithm to quantization errors in a finite-precision implementation. Furthermore, the authors demonstrate how block data adaptation and parallel-processing techniques facilitate the adaptive implementation of the CGM (for stationary data).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some alternative techniques for hardware address generators for digital signal processors
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Existing fast methods for generating the address sequences required for DSP (digital signal processing) applications are limited by use of both address arithmetic techniques employing ALUs (arithmetic logic units) and loop techniques. The alternative table-lookup method is limited due to table size, due either to the data block size or to the number of algorithms required. The alternatives presented by the author have the advantage of using counters which are potentially much faster than the adders utilized in ALU design. This is achieved without loss of generality other than restriction to a block size that is a power of two. In addition, avoidance of loops allows a fast pipeline approach to be used to further maximize speed. Parallel, parallel/serial, and serial approaches to this technique provide the designer with a number of cost/speed alternatives.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 2-D spectral factorization: classical and nonnegativity constrained
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The author reviews recent results which can contribute to the solution of the problem of nonnegativity-constrained spectral factorization for image reconstruction from autocorrelation data. This problem occurs in several high-frequency areas where only partial information about an image or signal is available. The remaining difficulties in obtaining a complete analytical solution to the problem and the manner in which those difficulties may be circumvented are also considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimization of a back bias generator for NMOS VLSI
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An optimized back bias generator was designed and implemented in the NS32332 32-bit microprocessor. A novel analysis method based on energy transfer in the charge pump circuit was used for better understanding of the circuit. The complete considerations, implementation, and the improved performance results are presented and discussed. The most important design consideration was to implement a very strong pump and to eliminate mechanisms that might cause instabilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The role of interpretation and diagnosis in signal processing
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A framework is proposed for adaptive signal processing that combines classical signal processing with adaptation criteria involving interpretation of the output signal and qualitative information about the classical signal processing itself. Interpretation of the output signal is achieved by expressing the signal at multiple levels of abstraction, capturing different levels of signal detail. A key aspect of the proposed framework is the computation of rich error descriptions by matching signal abstractions, as opposed to correlating numeric signals. Another key aspect is the encoding of qualitative information about the behavior of the classical signal processing component as processes that act on reference signal abstractions and produce output signal abstractions. A search is then conducted for the most plausible processes that explain the differences between the reference output and the actual output of the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transient stability evaluation of electric power systems using a fuzzy Perceptron algorithm
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The stability evaluation is performed rapidly by using a pattern recognition approach incorporating fuzzy membership functions. The algorithm is used to derive a classifier that classifies the system operating states as either stable or unstable. The feature selection is made by using a suitable function and a set of data representing the transient behavior of a network after the occurrence of specific large disturbances. The results obtained are illustrated by the analysis of a sample power system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of testable storage/logic arrays
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Storage/logic arrays (SLAs) represent an efficient structured logic array approach to the design of VLSI sequential logic circuits with low area overhead. The authors present an approach to testable SLA design which provides for detection of all missing device and stuck-at faults in addition to several broader classes of faults, including bridging and open line faults. Testable designs and test generation algorithms are given for both NMOS and static CMOS SLAs. An SLA augmented for testability is presented. The hardware costs are analyzed and the testing strategy is presented. The test sets are analyzed and are shown to provide high fault coverage over a large class of faults.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: geoADDICTION-flexible handling of complex geometries in IC layout tools
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A layout CAD (computer-aided design) system is presented that allows the flexible handling of different geometries to be used for IC design. The proposed parameterizable geometry model allows the user to make only the geometric features available to his CAD tools that are suitable for the current technology, hence providing the maximum efficiency for the tools' operation. Presently the system provides six geometry classes including circles and circle segments. The model has been designed so that it is easily expandable even to arbitrarily shaped geometric structures. The flexible geometry model is incorporated into ADDICTION, the control data management unit of the layout CAD system IMAGE.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parasitic-compensated building blocks for active switched-capacitor filters
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present novel stray-insensitive passive SC (switched-capacitor) building blocks which enable the realization of voltage transfer functions, voltage-to-current transfer functions, or the vector of voltage-to-current transfer functions. Such building blocks may be utilized in the synthesis of active SC filters. Circuits described by the voltage-to-current transfer functions may be used in the synthesis of SC networks comprising operational amplifiers, while the configurations described by the voltage transfer functions may be utilized in the design of SC circuits comprising unity-gain buffers. A number of design examples are provided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simultaneous amplitude and phase approximation for FIR filters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An FIR (finite-impulse response) filter design method with simultaneous amplitude and phase approximation is presented. Two components are proposed in this design method: simultaneous amplitude and phase interpolation in the passband and amplitude interpolation in the stopband. These interpolations are performed by the Remez exchange algorithm. The polynomials for the interpolations are generated by recurrence formulae, and the recurrence coefficients are calculated by a recursive method. The properties of the filters design with the simultaneous approximation are investigated and compared with properties of the exact linear and minimum-phase filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stability analysis of 2-D digital filters having second kind singularities-analog approach
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors show how stability analysis of a 2-D digital function can be carried out in the analog domain itself by testing the two-variable analog function from which the 2-D digital function is derived by the double bilinear transformation. This is particularly useful since one of the common methods of generating a 2-D digital function is by the application of double bilinear transformation on an appropriate two-variable analog function satisfying given frequency-response characteristics. By observing the conditions of the theorem, it may be stated that a necessary condition for stability or boundedness of a 2-D digital function is that the denominator of the corresponding 2-V analog function be scattering Hurwitz, as defined by A. Fetteweis (1984). Finally, these results have been used to study the existence of the double square integral in the analog domain.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: VLSI implementation of pipelined linear system solver
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A linear rotation-based algorithm without pivoting for solving linear system equations of the form Ax=b is presented. This algorithm modifies the conventional Gaussian elimination method and avoids the problems of numerical singularity and ill conditioning. It is shown that this algorithm can be implemented with a trapezoid-type array with n/sup 2//2+(n-2) processors, and a linear array with n processors, where n is the rank of this linear system. The former array performs the triangularization of matrix A using the modified linear rotation algorithm, and the latter array carries out the backward substitution for evaluating the solution of x. The computing time for solving linear system equations will be O(5n) time units. The architecture is simple, uniform, and regular, so it is well suited for implementation in VLSI.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling of analog networks by digital circuits
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The author discusses the problem of modelling an analog network by a digital circuit. A novel method is used to find bounds for the modelling error in the case of a given analog network. It is demonstrated that in certain cases a substantial error remains independently of the type of the digital system (FIR, recursive filters; minimum-phase, nonminimum-phase digital system) even if the degree of the system is extended to very high order (approaching infinity). Finally, methods are proposed which help to reduce this modelling limit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of the stochastic iteration algorithm and the dual sign algorithm in nonstationary environments
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An adaptive algorithm, called the dual sign algorithm (DSA), has been proposed recently to simplify the implementation of the widely-used stochastic iteration algorithm (SIA). Previous study has shown that, in stationary environments, the DSA, although simpler, exhibits faster convergence compared with the SIA, Here, computer simulation is used to compare the performance of the two algorithms in identifying some typical time-varying models. The results show that if both algorithms are designed to attain the same steady-state accuracy, the DSA always has a better tracking capability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A vector quantizer with short-time memory for digital image coding
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors propose a novel scheme of vector quantization with memory, named vector quantization with short-time memory (VQ-STM). The VQ-STM has two types of codebooks, a fixed-structure codebook whose codewords are kept unchanged, and a variable-structure codebook, which is defined as a subset of the fixed-structure codebook and whose structure is continually updated depending on the past behavior of the coder. The VQ-STM coder chooses the proper codebook between two codebooks for every input vector. The update of the variable-structure codebook is easily performed only by simple heuristics for maintaining a finite-length self-organizing sequential list which stores past coder outputs. The results of experimental simulations conducted on monochrome images demonstrate that significant compression gains can be achieved by enhancing the vector-quantization approach with the concept of short-time memory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SC-filter structures with reduced requirements on op-amp bandwidth and settling time
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Switched-capacitor (SC) filters designed from the state-variable equations of LC-filters with coupled-coil Brune sections have no time-continuous loops, and thus no positive feedback loops except through switched-capacitors. This leads to a reduced requirement on op-amp speed. By imposing certain restrictions on the coupled-coils inductance ratio, it is also possible to remove the summing capacitors, when the coupled-coil is embedded between single elements, which will further improve the sensitivity to the gain-bandwidth product. A fifth-order lowpass filter is taken as an example, showing the increased performance with this structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of dataflow program graphs
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An integrated approach to the modelling and performance evaluation of data-flow program graphs is developed by exploiting the similarities of such graphs to Petri nets (PNs). The basis of the methodology is a time-extended PN model, enhanced with data handling capabilities. Taking such an approach means that both data and control flow are combined in one model. Also, working in a PN-like form has the advantage that existing simulation programs (for time-extended PNs) can be easily modified for this novel application. Some examples are presented to illustrate the types of studies that can be carried out.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New stability conditions for matrix polynomials using a block-bidiagonal form
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present sufficient conditions for the stability of matrix polynomials based on algebraic properties of a block-bidiagonal form. This block-bidiagonal form corresponds to a state-space description of a multivariate feedback system associated with the matrix polynomial. An algorithm to obtain this block-bidiagonal form is presented. The stability results are based on the Lyapunov theory in conjunction with properties of this type of representation. Illustrative examples are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of multilevel mixed-mode simulator for LSI/VLSI circuits
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A prototype mixed-mode simulator (HYBRID) combines the speed of the conventional logic simulation with the accuracy of the block waveform relaxation method. A unified simulation time is introduced so that two subsimulators can work within one selective trace and next-event relaxation process. The simulator makes use of a multilevel macromodeling technique particularly well-suited to the block waveform relaxation. Logic and circuit types of macromodels are used. For typical logic MOS structures, a type specification algorithm based on the electrical loading effect (coupling of nodes) is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method to relax the design of active filters against large GB-variations
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A systematic method to design active filters to meet specified performance bounds over a wide range of values for the gain-bandwidth product (GB) is represented. The method finds a simplicial approximation to the acceptability region assuming ideal op amps and determines the minimum value of GB for which each of the boundary points is acceptable. The boundary point which allows the minimum value of GB is selected as optimal with respect to variations in GB. A balanced-structure filter simulating the operation of an LC ladder is considered as an example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A single-chip peer-relationship optical transceiver
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A CMOS peer-relationship optical transceiver has been fabricated, permitting bidirectional digital data transmission with one optical fiber. The IC, when used with a single LED, provides two full-duplex user data channels at 19.2 kb/s and 1200 b/s using time-division multiplexing of the optical signals. A block diagram of the optical transceiver is presented along with a simplified scheme of the analog receiver.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PENELOPE: a graph based logic simulator for MOS circuits
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A logic simulation tool called PENELOPE (Petri net logic performance evaluator) with precise delay estimation capabilities is presented. The simulator, which is particularly intended for CMOS circuits, makes use of a description of the logic network in terms of a Petri-net-like graph which implements the truth table of each logic operator and also processes the property of describing the evolution of the signal transitions in the network. Comparisons are made with other known simulators, showing that the performances are quite interesting especially in view of the precise modelling of time delays in the network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Verification of robustness of digital CMOS circuits
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A method to verify that a digital CMOS design is insensitive to variations in process parameters has been developed. During simulation the parts of a design which turn out to be sensitive to variations in detail are pointed out to the designer. This also gives an indication of what parts can be redesigned more aggressively to achieve better performance. Intrachip deviation and interchip deviation are treated separately to avoid inadequate uncertainty.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of doped channel heterostructure FETs and integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Describes a model used for the design of doped channel pseudomorphic AlGaAs/InGaAs/GaAs quantum-well HIGFETs and for the simulation of digital integrated circuits based on these devices. The model is based on the self-consistent quantum mechanical calculation of subbands and electron density in InGaAs quantum wells, obtained by solving a one-dimensional effective mass Schrodinger equation. Such a calculation shows that the potential barrier between the quasi-Fermi level in the channel and the bottom of the conduction band in the barrier layer is considerably larger for the doped-channel structure. This lowers the thermionic emission gate current of the doped channel device compared to the undoped channel structure, as confirmed by experimental data. The authors measured peak transconductance g/sub m/=471 mS/mm and peak l/sub dsat/=660 mA/mm in 0.6- mu m-gate doped-channel services. These results demonstrate the advantages of the DCHFET over the standard MODFET structure and their potential for high speed IC applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient algorithms for distributed query processing in star and extended-star networks
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Scheduling algorithms for processing queries in a star or extended-star network are presented. A relational database system is assumed, and the data transmission time for joins of attributes is the dominating factor in the query processing. The first algorithm STAR-RT for minimizing the response time of a star query is based on the principle of dynamic programming. The second one, STAR-CT, is an approximation algorithm also for processing a star query, but it aims at minimization of the total communication time. Two optimization subproblems are derived in connection with the query processing and STAR-CT is based on the strategies for solving these subproblems. The above algorithms are extended to those for more general query processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data pre-processing for high-resolution adaptive algorithms
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The inclusion of adaptive methods in high-resolution spectral estimation algorithms is considered. The generation of a complete family of spectral estimators from the normalized maximum-likelihood method (MLM) is discussed. It is shown how the generalized power MLM can be used to generate adaptive schemes for improving resolution. The authors propose the substitution of the conventional mean-square filtering error by quadratic objectives built as inner products of the coefficient error vector of the estimator filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A design technique for recursive linear time-varying digital filters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A reexamination of the frozen time approximation (FTA) is presented. It has been demonstrated that the FTA is still a viable option for the synthesis of LTV (linear-time-varying) filters. Since most applications of LTV filters are slowly varying the FTA is natural. Since optimization procedures on moderate-length LTV filters have prohibitive computational requirements, the FTA is efficient in comparison. Improvements have been proposed to synthesize FTA-based filters which are more accurate than those synthesized by the available optimization techniques at a small fraction of the computational load. It is concluded that it is reasonable to consider that other techniques for LTV filter synthesis should be implemented only on those quickly varying filters for which all FTA-based techniques fail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Random signal applications in biomedical engineering
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors show three examples of biomedical applications essentially based on random processes, (1) the evaluation of saccadic eye movement disorders under randomized visual stimuli, (2) the detection and analysis of turbulent sounds produced by turbulent blood flow due to intracranial aneurysm and arteriovenous malformation, and (3) the use of 1/f fluctuations to control transcutaneous electrical stimulation for pain relief. With respect to these examples, the role of randomness and the appropriate circuit systems are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Inverse star-mesh transformation and network-element-value observability
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The linear transistor resistor network fault diagnosis problem is considered. The difference between the analog fault diagnosis problem and the network element value observability problem is made clear. It is shown that the network element values are observable if all network element values are determined uniquely by the measured data with the accessible nodes and by the network topology. After discussing the two terminal resistor network, the authors consider some sufficient conditions for the transistor network to be observable. A method for calculating the element value for a multi-star inaccessible network is proposed. The method presented is fundamentally derived from the special property of submatrices of the indefinite admittance matrix for the network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of simultaneous nonlinear algebraic equations
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: J.B. Moore's (J. Assoc. Comp. Math., vol.14, p.311-5, 1976) method of solving a single-variable algebraic equation is generalized to a method for multivariable simultaneous algebraic equations. The proposed method makes use of an objective function similar to the Lyapunov function, but it has multiple-zero points corresponding to the solution of the original algebraic equation. Using the proposed method, all solutions of a simultaneous nonlinear algebraic equation with complex coefficients are obtained for both real and complex roots.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of the block Jacobi method to piecewise-linear analysis of DC diode-transistor networks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The application of the block Jacobi method to piecewise-linear analysis of DC diode-transistor circuits is discussed. The problem of convergence of the method is considered in detail. Sufficient conditions guaranteeing the convergence of the iterative process to a unique solution for each initial guess are formulated. Some weaker conditions relating to the solvability and computation of the circuits are developed. The efficiency of the block Jacobi method is analyzed. The method has been tested and compared with other well-known algorithms of piecewise-linear analysis, such as J. Katzenelson's (1965) and Newton-Raphson's algorithm. Some advantages of the method are indicated and suggestions concerning the computation process are made. Several numerical examples are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A self-testing systolic module for VLSI DSP applications
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors propose a novel concurrent error-detection scheme for error detection in VLSI arrays. The proposed scheme is called LOED (logarithm-based online error detection) and is based on the use of logarithmic coding. This scheme is analyzed and its implementation details are described. Fault coverage and hardware overhead of the scheme are also discussed. The application of LOED to the convolution problem is described, and the advantages of LOED are enumerated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multistage approach to narrowband digital filters
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An efficient multistage structure is presented for narrowband finite-impulse response (FIR) filters. The structure consists of cascading FIR stages. Each stage operates at the same input sampling rate while its filter's sampling rate is the power of the input rate. Such an arrangement can greatly reduce the number of multipliers without increasing the complexity of the filter. The optimum number of stages can be easily determined. The quantization error is also analyzed. Several examples are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of computational methods for MESFET intermodulation characteristics
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A systematic comparison of a variety of approaches to the numerical calculation of GaAs MESFET intermodulation characteristics is presented, with particular emphasis on large-signal operation. The methods evaluated include direct time-domain analysis, harmonic-balance, Volterra series, and transfer characteristic methods. The advantages and limitations of each technique are assessed in relation to a realistic distributed MESFET power amplifier. It is concluded that the time-domain technique requires the minimum number of assumptions and produces intermodulation characteristics with considerable structural behaviour.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMG signal discrimination for controlling walking functions in paraplegics under electrical stimulation
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe the use of electromyographic (EMG) signatures for controlling functional electrical stimulation (FES) in upper-motor-neuron paraplegics to enable them to walk with the help of a walker, or in some cases with the help of elbow-support crutches. It is shown that the above-lesion and below-lesion EMG controls both serve complementary and crucial roles in total FES control. It is also shown that below-lesion response EMG control of stimulation-levels can play a crucial role in FES, regardless of above-lesion EMG control. This can be done in conjunction with other control methods such as hand-switch control or pelvic thrust.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Extraction of BJT model parameters with a new strategy improving speed and accuracy
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A method of extracting bipolar junction transistor model parameters is presented which utilized the SPICE 2G-6 approach. The parameter-extraction technique is based on minimizing a nonlinear objective function, producing a least-squares fit of the model equations to a set of measured device characteristics. A strategic combination of the direct search optimization method and the variable metric algorithm is employed. A special strategy improving the speed of calculating the objective function during optimization is proposed. A model modification is also presented that gives high accuracy of the fit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of GaAs-FET noise properties at VHF-/UHF-frequencies
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A noise equivalent circuit for two different kinds of GaAs FETs is presented which is based on DC- and S-parameter measurements. It is verified by noise measurements between 50 and 200 MHz. Optimum source impedances were measured for the GaAs-FETs GAT 1/010 and NE 244. The calculated values lie well within the uncertainty limits of the measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An iterative technique for polynomial factorization
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An iterative technique is presented for the factorization (splitting) of a real-coefficient polynomial into two lower-degree polynomials, one being the complex conjugate of the other. The algorithm is simple and suitable for programming, and monotonic convergence is guaranteed. A typical application is the determination of the reflection coefficient of a lossless network from its transmission coefficient. A numerical example is given which demonstrates that the method is considerably faster than a more conventional technique based on root extraction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SAW filters for radio communication systems
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A review is presented of full-custom SAW (surface-acoustic-wave) components for radio systems, e.g., for cordless telephone, mobile radio, digital radio relay, satellite radio, and spread-spectrum communication. Design, results and applications are discussed, including the comparison with alternative filter techniques. Low-loss filters are presented with insertion losses down to 2 dB; bandpass filters with ripples less than 0.1 dB and 1 degrees , and stopband rejections better than 60 dB; delay lines up to 2.5 GHz; SAW oscillators at a fundamental of 2 GHz with phase noise of 100 dBc/Hz; and SAW convolvers with about -60 dBm efficiency and 160 MHz bandwidth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new configuration for SAW resonator based oscillators
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel oscillator design technique based on two-port SAW resonators is described. This technique makes it possible to measure the most critical oscillator features, i.e., resonator loaded Q/insertion loss and amplifier phase/amplitude characteristic. This procedure ensures the achievement of a good tradeoff between specific oscillator performances like FM phase noise and frequency tuning span, with the additional feature of a stable, stress-free frequency setting. Experimental results for several oscillator prototypes in the 591-1090-MHz range are reported. An important feature of the proposed configuration is open-loop testability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Exact analysis of non-ideal SC networks through op amps asymptotic modeling
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A compact systematic analysis method to obtain closed-form expressions for the z-domain transfer functions of switched-capacitor (SC) circuits with finite gain-bandwidth (GB)-product op amps is presented. This procedure allows exact frequency analysis of general SC circuits without imposing any restriction in the ratio between GB and clock frequencies and, is based on the modeling of each op amp by a suitable SC subcircuit with its own clock frequency, which is made to tend toward infinity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Contingency-constrained reactive power planning and scheduling
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe a software package that has been created to solve the contingency-constrained reactive power flow problem. A methodology is presented which aims to provide an effective tool for the planning and scheduling of reactive power under a set of defined contingencies. The proposed methodology uses a decomposition/coordination scheme to solve the reactive power scheduling problem. The set of equations, composed of the base case and specified contingencies, is partitioned in such a way that a dynamic set of the most sensitive control variables is associated with each contingency. A parallel-processing scheme produces the required solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performances of bandpass cascaded SC filters with reduced pole-Qs
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The multiple-critical-pole equiripple rational (MCPER) transfer functions are compared with the elliptic transfer functions in the design of bandpass cascaded-biquad switched-capacitor (SC) filters. Filters designed using the two classes of functions are investigated in terms of bandpass sensitivity, total capacitance, group delay, and noise. The results show that MCPER transfer functions make it possible to design SC filters with superior performances, in particular with lower bandpass sensitivity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer aided double matching via parametric representation of Brune functions
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A novel method of broadbanding which utilizes the parametric representation of Brune functions is applied to double-matching problems. Examples are presented to exhibit the use of the parametric-broadband matching procedure. The results obtained are compared with those obtained by the real frequency-direct computational technique. It is concluded that the real frequency-direct computational and the parametric methods of broadband matching yield similar results with the same complexity of the matching networks. On the other hand, if the complexity of the equalizer is increased, the parametric approach offers high numerical stability with less computation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A highly parallel block processing algorithm for LS FIR filtering
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A highly parallel algorithm for least-squares FIR (finite-impulse response) filtering is presented. The algorithm is of the covariance type and can be performed on a linear array of O(p) processors with p being the order of the filter. The required time is 4p ( tau /sub 1/+ tau /sub 2/+ tau /sub 3/) with tau /sub 1/, tau /sub 2/, tau /sub 3/ being the time units for division, multiplication and addition respectively. Initialization is performed in N( tau /sub 2/+ tau /sub 3/) units with N being the length of the data block.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SYNCOM-the procedure of linear network synthesis and its application in CMOS filter design
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The author presents an algorithm for solving nonlinear equations obtained by coefficient matching. This synthesis method is very effective in continuous-time CMOS filter design. The advantages of the proposed method in comparison with the Newton method are shown. A procedure called SYNCOM has been written in Pascal to implement the algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stochastic control techniques applied to chaotic nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Chaotic nonlinear systems exhibit behavior similar in many respects to noise-corrupted systems. The use of stochastic control techniques, in particular a state estimator based on the Kalman filter, enables implementation of a control algorithm for control of these systems whose performance is improved with respect to that obtainable by use of a controller utilizing only the conditional mean of the system state vector. The method is applied to two typical chaotic nonlinear systems, and their behavior with control is explored numerically. It is shown that chaotic nonlinear systems appear to retain their chaotic dynamics when control signals are applied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Suspended substrate strip line filters with flat delay
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A procedure has been developed for designing narrowband suspended substrate stripline (SSS) microwave filters in the comb form. The design is based on an even-degree lowpass lumped prototype network of a ladder nature. An auxiliary coupling has been introduced to flatten the delay characteristics. A frequency transformation has been worked out to transform the characteristics of the lumped filter to the microwave region. Explicit formulas have been derived for physical dimensions of the SSS lines from the relationships between the characteristic admittance and the static capacitances of the lines and the element values of the prototype network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bit-rate reduction for high-quality audio signals using floating-point wave digital filters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A source coding scheme for the low-bit-rate transmission of high-quality audio signals (16-bit quantizing resolution) is discussed. Encoding with approximately 3 bits per sample is possible without perceptible impairment of the signal quality. A subband coder with 27 bands is obtained by a cascade of digital filters implemented with floating-point arithmetic; the bandwidths are chosen according to the psychoacoustical 'critical bands' of the human ear, and the signals in the subbands are quantized with variable bit allocation depending on the masking threshold. If conventional digital filters are used in the arrangement, large parasitic oscillations and forced-response instabilities may occur. In the case of an implementation using lattice wave digital filters with a bireciprocal characteristic function, no precautions need to be taken to avoid instabilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance improvement of all digital phase-locked loop with adaptive multilevel-quantized phase comparator
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A type of phase comparator for digital phase-locked loops, called the adaptive multilevel quantized phase comparator (AMPC), is proposed. The phase comparison characteristics of this proposed comparator operate adaptively, by shifting them up or down and by changing the scale, following the frequency deviation and the phase jitter of the input signals. The performances of the AMPC and the loop with AMPC are obtained theoretically and verified by computer simulation. As a result, the loop with this AMPC has a much wider locking-range and a much better jitter suppression effect than those of the conventional loop, as well as an improved steady-state phase error.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polyphase FIR filters for the demodulation of chrominance signals
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The author presents a scheme and its polyphase FIR (finite-impulse-response) filter implementation for the demodulation of chrominance signal into in-phase and quadrature-phase components. The scheme applies to any system whose sampling frequency is related to the color subcarrier frequency by a rational factor. The authors presents the criteria for choosing a sampling frequency for the digitization of a TV studio signal and addresses the issue of digital demodulation of the chrominance component in a composite video signal.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An extension to the lossless inverse scattering problem and application to spectral approximation
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The author proposes an extension to the classical lossless inverse scattering (LIS) problem and points out its potential use in spectral approximation in the areas of signal modelling and model reduction for optimal control. He presents a solution consisting of tree steps, the first of which is the classical LIS-algorithm. The second step is a simple transformation of the data and the last step is an application of the multichannel LIS-algorithm. The algorithm is essentially recursive and thus computationally very attractive. Illustrative examples have been worked out.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Image compression and coding, with emphasis on polygon based techniques and representation
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Data-compression methods can be divided into two main categories, reversible and irreversible. A brief summary of the techniques in both categories is given. In addition, irreversible methods for conversion from raster representation to polygon-based representation are described. One technique is based on global processing and representation, while the other is based on local methods. Examples of pictures processed with both methods are shown, and the similarities and differences are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A sparing SC filter design approach with reduced transmission zeros
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A systematic switched-capacitor (SC) filter design method that satisfies a set of frequency specifications while its implementation requires less total capacitance than the conventional design using the bilinear mapping is presented. The design approach is based on: (i) a prewarping scheme for different mappings of the 1/s and 1/s/sup 2/ terms of each biquadratic factor forming the transfer function; (ii) strategic addition of zeros at z=-1; and (iii) iterative modification of the frequency responses rendering different transfer functions that eventually satisfy the original frequency design specifications. A detailed algorithm is discussed together with an examples showing the attractive properties of the proposed method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An approach to design totally self-checking checker for the 1-out-of-3 code at transistor level
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors propose a TSC (totally self-checking) checker in MOS technology for 1/3 code based on a set of physical defects. Although it is not possible to design such a checker at the gate level, both analysis and computer simulation show that the proposed checker is a TSC checker for 1/3 code with respect to the given set of faults at the transistor level. Such a checker can be easily incorporated in self-checking design of VLSI chips.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The mixed transversal and ladder adaptive filters with pulse order updates
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Mixed transversal and ladder (MITAL) adaptive filter structures of exact least-square type are presented, which can be treated either as transversal forms or as ladders forms to meet requirements of different applications. Owing to the purely order-recursive characteristics, error propagation is eliminated and performance degradation in the conventional fast recursive-least-squares RLS algorithms, caused by limited-precision effects, does not occur in the structures. The outstanding numerical performance of the proposed adaptive filters is illustrated by computer simulations and comparison to other well-known fast recursive-least-squares structures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An application of equivalent transformations for analysis of nonuniform transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The author presents an efficient method of equivalent transformations for analyzing the stationary phenomena in a system of distributed-parameter circuits with jump heterogeneity and arbitrary boundary conditions. A change of the electrical line-length and a transposition of the independent sources along the line lead to an elementary lumped circuit which allows for a simple description of the phenomena in the original system. The method makes it possible to reduce a system of lumped and distributed parameters to an elementary lumped-parameter circuit consisting of active two-terminal networks. The method can be applied to the analysis of a system of interconnected active and passive uniform lines and lumped elements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A speed enhancing architecture for a floating point signal processor
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In contrast to fixed-point arithmetic, floating-point arithmetic requires more steps for a given operation, which normally slows down the execution speed of a floating-point processor. A special hardware architecture for minimizing this problem is proposed. The processor is a four-address machine with Harvard architecture. A two-level pipelining is introduced., i.e. fetching of operands and storing of the result are done in parallel with arithmetic calculations. This pipelining is invisible for the programmer, because a special register allows the access to the result of the last operation. The fundamental arithmetic operation is D=A+B*C.Addressing of operands is either direct or indexed with base offset and auto-modification. All of these addressing modes can be used independently for all of the four addresses in one instruction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the use of a linear phase lattice structure in Prony's method for spectral line estimation
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: It is known that Prony's method for spectral line estimation requires a filter coefficient symmetric property. Taking advantage of this property, the authors show that the frequencies of the spectral lines can be determined from the reflection coefficients of a cascaded orthogonal FIR (finite-impulse response) lattice algorithm with the data processed in an adaptive mode. An adaptive algorithm based on the LMS criterion has been derived. Simulations indicate that this algorithm can be applied in the estimation of spectral lines in noise. The proposed approach has the advantage of the robustness of lattice modeling techniques, and thereby avoids the numerical problems usually associated with Prony's method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wavefront computations of band-limited matrix operations on a torus data-driven array: FEM-TORUS
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Let A be an N*n nonsingular matrix of bandwidth 2w+1 (n>>w) and b be an n*1 vector. The authors design of a torus array arrangement of data-driven processors of size (2w+2)*(2w+2), on which the diagonal data band of the extended matrix (Alb) is wrapped around in (n+w+1)/(2w+2) layers. They also present a matrix-data mapping onto the torus surface and wavefront-driven algorithms of three matrix operations essential in solution processes of a linear system Ax=b often arising in finite-element analysis: (1) triangulation by Givens plane rotations on the basis of the Sameh-Kuck annihilation scheme; (2) backward substitution for obtaining a Gaussian solution; and (3) matrix-vector multiplication that appears as a basic step in iterative improvement of the initial Gaussian solution. The system is named FEM-TORUS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bounds on signal delay in RC mesh networks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The author addresses the problem of estimating the inverse of the node-conductance matrix R of a resistive network as in MOS LSI. The main result is the definition of two bounding matrices. Since the derivation of these matrices depends solely on Tellegen's theorem, the result is therefore applicable to all resistive networks that obey Kirchoff's laws, whether the networks are linear or nonlinear, time-invariant or time-varying, reciprocal or nonreciprocal. It is observed that the upper bound matrix tends to be closer to R if the resistive network is tree-like. Likewise, the lower bound matrix tends to be closer to R if the resistive network consists mainly of parallel connections of identical resistors. From the bounding matrices, bounds on the delays can be obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A non-minimal wire length algorithm for complex routing problems
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A routing algorithm is presented which is based on the general (original) Lee-model and can be used for a wide range of design rules, pad (contact) sizes and shapes, and variable track widths and separations. Different design rules can be assigned to ground and power lines, signals, and special rules can be applied to selected modes. Via pads (contact holes) are inserted automatically. The connections are not of minimal length; their shape is optimized by a sophisticated path function in such a way that the spread of wires is nearly homogeneous in all phases of the routing process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time-domain analysis methods for switching convertors
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Two algorithms are presented for a time-domain analysis of a switching convertor which is replaceable with a piecewise-linear system. One of these algorithms is for the transient state analysis and the other is for the steady-state analysis. Both algorithms use eigenvalue and eigenvector calculations of the matrix. By using these algorithms, the analysis can be carried out more rapidly and accurately than the existing analyses using standard fixed or variable step-size integration methods. This is demonstrated in a Cuk convertor analysis by comparing the results of the proposed method with those of a Hamming method (a variable-step integration method), and SPICE2.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive simulated annealing used in the synthesis of switched capacitor filters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a computer program called MASFIL for the synthesis of switched-capacitor (SC) filters. MASFIL allows the user to synthesize filters with classic and nonclassic transfer functions. The program handles the nonclassic cases with an adaptive simulated annealing algorithm. The algorithm optimizes the transfer functions to satisfy the user-given frequency response and group delay specifications. MASFIL runs on an IBM/PC/AT and gives as output a hierarchical schematic and a netlist file. The main advantages of using MASFIL have been the drastic reduction in design time (from weeks to hours) and a more effective usage of silicon area because of the capability of implementing multirate switched capacitor filters with nonclassic transfer functions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Switched-capacitor filter networks derived from general parameter bandpass LC ladder networks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Extensions to two previously published switched-capacitor (SC) bandpass filter synthesis techniques are presented. These techniques are the impedance scaling method of R.B. Datar and A.S. Sedra (IEEE Trans. Circuits Syst., vol.CAS-30, p.888-898, Dec. 1983) and the mode simulation method for bandpass filter design of K. Martin and A.S. Sedra (IEEE Trans. Circuits Syst., vol.CAS-27, June 1980). The main focus of the present study is on the SC circuit simulation of a set of circuit describing equations derived from arbitrary general parameter bandpass LC ladder networks. An eight-order design example has been used to illustrate the extension to the two design methods. Although this example requires more op amps than the filter order, both designs have been shown to possess low sensitivity to component variations and a relatively low total capacitance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systolic model and systolic geometry
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The lack of a precise model for systolic algorithms has been hindering progress in the automatic synthesis of systolic arrays. The author proposes a model that encompasses a very large class of algorithms but is still restrictive enough so that mappings of such algorithms onto systolic architectures whose time performance is within a known factor of the optimum may be generated systematically. The issue of the determination of parallel schedules and allocation schemes is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stochastic versus deterministic concepts in adaptive systems design
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Adaptive systems for signal processing can be characterized from both stochastic and deterministic viewpoints. A review of the underlying optimality principles, emphasizing the local aspects of adaptive algorithms is given. Time variance is introduced as an explicit concept of algorithm design; and a solution in terms of a coefficient vector predictor is presented. Finally, the question of robustness of adaptive systems is explored with respect to numerical stability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stability of multidimensional systems: overview and new results
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Most of the stability results of 2-D discrete systems using the Lyapunov method and the state-space approach are reviewed. The stability of m-dimensional systems is studied through classification of various regions of analyticity, and several theorems and algebraic tests for checking these regions are reviewed. A stability test is presented for two-dimensional systems using the bilinear continued fraction expansion. Numerical examples are presented which support the results. The present study is pertinent to the analysis of the stability of two-dimensional filters, used extensively in image processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assignment of system zeros using a new numerically stable algorithm (multivariable systems)
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a numerically stable algorithm for assigning a prescribed set of zeros to a linear system described by a state-space model (A, B, C, D). The method is based on the generalized Schur form of the system matrix, and the implicitly shifted QR algorithm. The approach imposes no restrictions on the state-space model, and does not require computation of the zeros of the original system. Numerical properties of the algorithm are discussed and examples are given to illustrate its performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A construction method of Lyapunov functions for piecewise-linear systems
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors propose a Lyapunov-function construction method, giving the asymptotic stability region of a piecewise-linear (PWL) dynamical system. Lyapunov functions are constructed by connecting quadratic functions on each divided region, so that the computational tasks to obtain the asymptotic stability region are simplified. Also given is a simple condition according to which the asymptotic stability region of the PWL system is included in that of original nonlinear system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generalized algorithm of short discrete cosine transform
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The author proposes a generalized short algorithm for the calculation of the discrete cosine transform of data arrays with a length equal to an integral power of two, plus 1. It is shown that there is a class of algorithms which make it possible to perform the necessary calculations with more speed and accuracy, and with fewer arithmetic operations and memory accesses, than the previously known algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of equivalent precision dedicated FFT processors
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A study of the quantization noise in FFT (fast Fourier transform) processors is undertaken with the purpose of comparing several possible Si implementations. Simulations are presented to validate theoretical results and to derive corrected formulas, that predict simulation results within 0.5 dB. Finally, a comparative study shows that application-specific integrated circuits using fixed-point arithmetic with truncation represent the best compromise for real-time integrated FFTs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pipeline implementation of Pisarenko's method for high resolution 2-D spectrum estimation
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a computationally efficient 2-D spectrum estimation method using three spectrum estimations corresponding to the horizontal, vertical, and diagonal directions under the assumption that the 2-D data arrays are represented as 2-D sinusoids in white noise. Polynomials corresponding to the z-transforms of each trigonometric identity equations represent linear-phase FIR (finite-impulse-response) filters. Using the property, the authors develop a modified Pisarenko method which achieves faster convergence with less computational complexity when compared to the original Pisarenko method. It is also shown that the modified 2-D Pisarenko method is unbiased. Finally, an asynchronous pipelined array chain architecture to increase computational throughput and parallelism is developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SC networks with zero amplifier finite gain sensitivity
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A compensation method is proposed which eliminates the operational amplifier (OA) finite-gain effect completely in discrete switched-capacitor (SC) integrators. The transfer functions of nearly all stray-insensitive two-phase SC networks can be made to have zero sensitivity to OA gains. At the same time, DC error voltage and low-frequency noise components of the amplifier can be eliminated or reduced dramatically. The technique simplifies amplifier design and increases the high-frequency capability of SC networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Positioning of group delay sections with an LC ladder and the effects of transformations
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The problem of group-delay specification and approximation in computer-aided filter design is considered. The author illustrates some of the necessary extensions required to the Z-plane approach to cover the extraction of complex quartets. The extended procedure evaluates the input immittance at a complex frequency, finds the component values for the complex section, and calculates the remaining immittance to a sufficiently good accuracy. The transformation to the bridged-tee form is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of number theory to structurally passive digital filters
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The Givens planar rotator is a basic component of a structurally passive digital filter. The realization of this element by a residue number system is discussed, with particular attention given to the elimination of multiplications by applying the isomorphism between the modular multiplication and addition. The authors also propose a possible scheme for extending the dynamic range of the rotator, based on the Chinese remainder theorem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a defect-tolerant and fully testable PLA
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a defect-tolerant and fully testable programmable logic array (PLA) that is based on dynamic redundancy, allowing for the repair of a defective chip. Special emphasis is placed on the location of defects inside a PLA. The repair process consists of replacing a defect product term by a programmable spare one.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high-speed 22-bit floating-point digital signal processor: the FSPU
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors describe the FSPU, which is a single-chip 22-bit signal and speech processor. The FSPU is based on a novel processing unit that achieves very high computation throughputs, while using floating-point arithmetic to achieve wide dynamic range and high precision. The developed architecture is intended to go beyond the limits of the standard general-purpose digital signal-processing implementations and to make floating-point signal processing more attractive. Testability, control flexibility, and area were strongly emphasized. A 3- mu m CMOS prototype has been realized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A pipelined signal processor for real-time generation of radar images
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A special-purpose processor architecture for real-time spaceborne synthetic aperture radar strip-mapping mode data processing is described. This processor uses the fast Fourier transform (FFT) correlation technique to perform the range pulse compression function, and a hybrid FFT time-domain finite-impulse-response filtering approach to perform the range migration correction and azimuth pulse compression functions. The processing functions of this processor are pipelined to gain high throughput. This processor has the advantages of (1) being very efficient in both arithmetic computation and range migration correction and (2) requiring minimal control complexity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modification of a radio link system from analog to digital
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors describe the modifications in converting an analog radio-link system for use in digital communication. The existing analog system uses frequency modulation at the 6-GHz band to transmit 1860 frequency-division-multiplexed (FDM) voice channels. The baseband units of this system are replaced by digital circuits without any changes in radio-frequency sections. The system can transmit and receive 34 Mb/s (480 channels) standard third-level PCM (pulse code modulated) data in HDB3 or NRZ format. Although the modification reduces the bandwidth efficiency, it is an attractive choice for converting the analog communication network to digital in rural areas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Lower bounds for the stability margin of linear discrete systems based on the weighted performance criteria
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Lower bounds for the stability margin of linear discrete systems computed from impulse response measurements are presented. These bounds are based on the connection between the weighted performance criteria and the Lyapunov equation. It is shown that positive definite matrices satisfying the Lyapunov equation for a stable system with unknown parameters can be computed from impulse response measurements. The lower bounds for the stability margin can be obtained from the eigenvalues of these matrices. The properties of the method presented are discussed and it is shown that the lower bounds can be improved by increasing the order of the weighting factor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fundamental factorization theorems for rational matrices over complex or real fields
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: It is shown that any complex rational matrix G(s) can be factorized over the complex field as a minimal product of n complex rational matrices, each of which has McMillan degree 1, where n is the McMillan degree of G(s). When confined to the real field, G(s) with real coefficient can be factorized as a minimal product of a sequence of real rational matrices with McMillan degree 1 or 2, where the McMillan degrees of the factors add up to n. The results obtained thus settle a long-standing conjecture over the factorization of rational matrices. The proofs of these fundamental factorization theorems are constructive. Therefore, by following the suggested numerical procedures, all the factors over the real or the complex fields can be easily obtained. It is noted that the results obtained can be applied in the design of multiport or multichannel filters which can be realized in a VLSI implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Subfilter approach for designing efficient FIR filters
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Recently, several special filter structures, together with the design methods, have been proposed for reducing the cost of implementation of FIR (finite-impulse response) filters. The authors review some of the techniques based on the use of subfilters as basic building blocks. There are basically two different subfilter approaches, the first one using different subfilters and the second one using identical subfilters. The authors concentrate on the design of lowpass filters, even though most methods considered can be applied equally well to the design of other types of filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A tutorial on multirate digital filter banks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A number of topics in multirate digital signal processing, such as decimation and interpolation, polyphase structures, power-complementary and Mth band filters, and digital filter banks are reviewed. Maximally decimated digital filter banks are emphasized, and the problem of perfect reconstruction reviewed. The role of FIR (finite-impulse-response) lossless systems in this context is also reviewed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Floating-point signal processing-arithmetic, roundoff-noise, and limit cycles
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The number of representation and the range of floating-point numbers is treated for floating-point signal processing. The addition and multiplication operations which are most important for digital signal processing are explained in detail including the necessary normalization operations. Quantization errors in terms of the probability densities of the relative errors are analyzed in detail for roundoff-quantization, two's-complement-truncation, and magnitude-truncation. The roundoff-noise is determined for a single quantizer and for complex signal processing flowgraphs. The problem of limit cycles is discussed briefly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High-speed analog-to-digital conversion with GaAs technology: prospects, trends and obstacles
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors addresses the prospects for widespread use of GaAs technology for analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion, the technological and design trends for improved A/D realizations, and the obstacles to the realization of higher speed and resolution.
