Experimental results which illustrate the performance of the method are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signal delay in RC networks with floating capacitors
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A scheme is presented for the estimation of signal delay in RC networks with floating capacitors. The scheme involves finding signal delays in the network with the floating capacitors either replaced by open circuits or short circuits. Preliminary experiments have shown that the scheme is viable and could be used to build an efficient RC simulator that handles RC networks with floating capacitors. The results are pertinent to the use of linear lumped RC networks in timing simulators to model MOS digital circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A synthesis of low-sensitivity digital filters using T-cascade of wave lattice sections
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors propose new low-sensitivity digital filter structures which are also suited for pipeline processing. The approach involves the synthesis of digital two-port circuits with structurally induced losslessness. The structures are synthesized by factoring lossless scattering matrices, and constructed using the T-cascade connection of basic sections, instead of the Pi -cascade connection. Each lossless factor is realized by a first- or second-order wave digital lattice filter. The proposed structures can realize the amplitude responses of any given transfer functions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast on-chip delay estimation for cell-based emitter coupled logic
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An effort was made to produce fast, but accurate, estimates of best and worst-case delay for on-chip emitter-coupled logic (ECL) nets. The effort consisted of two major parts: (1) macromodeling of ECL logic gates acting as both sources and loads; and (2) delay estimation for individual nets using the gate macromodel parameters and RC tree models for metal interconnect. Both of these functions have been extensively tested on an industrial ECL process and cell (i.e., logic gate) library. It is noted that the success of a macromodeling approach relies on repetitive use of members of a library of modeled cells. A fixed computational cost (several CPU hours per cell) is paid to obtain simplified macromodel parameter values. Resultant timing estimates are typically within 5-10% of SPICE and are obtained roughly three orders of magnitude more quickly than SPICE.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison between CELP and MPLPC at 8 kbit/s for mobile communications
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Two analysis-by-synthesis schemes, with a different excitation structure, have been optimized for a bit-rate of 8 kb/s. The codebook excited linear predictive (CELP) coder and the multi-pulse linear predictive coder (MPLPC) were considered. Some improvements over conventional coders have been achieved by computing the long-term parameters by a closed-loop procedure and using a split vector quantization of line spectrum pair coefficients for the short-term spectrum representation. The complexity of the two schemes has been considered as a design constraint and the result is the implementation feasibility of both algorithms with standard floating-point digital signal processors. Both coders are shown to provide very high speech quality without transmission errors. The present study is pertinent to the development of the pan-European digital mobile radio system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generation of transconductance grounded capacitor filters by signal-flow graph simulation of LC-ladders
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The methods are presented for generating active simulations of LC-ladders, based on signal-flow graphs. Both methods use only tunable transconductance elements and grounded capacitors. Furthermore, all transconductances except possibly one are identical and all capacitors are grounded, making the approach extremely convenient for integration with automated systematic design procedures and dense layout. SPICE simulations of the circuits with actual CMOS transconductance have been used to verify the performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimum implementation of a multistage IIR SC bandpass decimator for a voiceband analogue interface system
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel methodology has been developed for the design of multistage infinite impulse response switched-capacitor decimators with optimum implementation. The approach uses a cascade of only IIR SC decimator building blocks as a means of obtaining minimum-order structures for high selectivity filtering requirements with very large factors of sampling rate reduction. The strategy for reducing the sampling rate is determined in conjunction with the pole-zero pairing to achieve relaxed speed requirements for the operational amplifiers together with reduced capacitance spread and total capacitor area. This is demonstrated for an SC bandpass decimator which virtually eliminates the need for costly on-chip continuous-time filters, thus making it extremely attractive for integrated-circuit implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: From recursive algorithm to parallel VLSI accelerator: a hierarchical design system with testbed
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An instance of a design method allowing the interactive mapping of certain recursive algorithms to nearest-neighbor SMD (single-instruction, multiple data stream) processor arrays is considered. The design system accepts certain sequential iterative algorithms and aids the designer in obtaining any desired fixed size parallel or pipeline (VLSI) implementation. The authors give a concise description of a prototype design system that supports the mapping trajectory, including the VLSI design of the processor elements, as well as the testing of the functional behavior of both an individual processor and the processor array in a real-world environment. An illustrative example is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A nonlinear PIN diode model for use in multi-diode microwave and RF communication circuit simulation
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A nonlinear p-i-n diode model suitable for use in microwave and RF communication circuit simulation is presented. The circuit nonlinear transfer functions are computed and verified with experimental distortion measurements on series and shunt reflective attenuators. These transfer functions are useful in circuit and device simulation since they are algebraic in nature and require minimal computation time. The model presented is applicable to both gallium arsenide and silicon p-i-n diodes, in packaged, beam lead or chip form.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PRINT methodology: a compilation approach for cell library generation
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present a fast design methodology of CMOS digital ICs. A compilation of cell library using the parametrizable, resizable, and independent of the technology (PRINT) generator allows full custom implementation of ASICs (application-specific integrated circuits) using high-level defined symbolic custom cells. Application of this generator to the development of an industrial ASIC is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of high-speed asynchronous communication ports for VLSI multicomputer nodes
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present the design of synchronizing communication ports for a communication coprocessor chip. These ports minimize the probability of synchronization failure and support communication at a very high rate relative to the limits of the implementation technology. The scheme presented does not require any lines in the link in addition to the data lines and does not require byte-per-byte handshaking. The design includes a synchronizer and a high-performance FIFO (first-in, first-out) buffer. This design is particularly well-suited for VLSI implementation and, for a given technology, can support higher communication speeds than previous synchronizer designs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Silicon compiler generates fast multipliers embedded in data path
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors introduce a multiplier generator presenting two major novel features: Booth/Wallace multipliers can be embedded in a data path, and a design strategy based on intelligent silicon compilation allows user-directed detailed refinement. This generator produces a smaller, faster, and safer design than an equivalent one manually completed. Moreover, it generates Csa-tree/Booth multipliers embedded in data paths, which has seldom been achieved, especially for big multipliers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Logic gate formed neuron type processing element
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present the design of neuron-type circuit elements based on logic circuits, mainly NAND gates. Three types of subcircuits were introduced, one called the cell body with its dendritic inputs, another representing the axon base, and the final one mimicking the axon. The resulting design was an asynchronous sequential circuit. This neuron-type processing element (NTPE) computes the sum of binary weighted input pulses incorporating temporal as well as spatial summation and thresholding. This process has been accomplished by introducing a time constraint variable in the operation of the NTPE. With the availability of VLSI techniques to implement these NTPEs, full neural-type systems, including computers, can be conceived and constructed using presently available IC technology. Alternatively, they can be assembled from off-the-shelf logic circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency domain modeling of dual-input/multiple-output quadratic systems with general random inputs
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A digital method of estimating linear and quadratic transfer functions of a dual-input/multiple-output quadratically nonlinear system with general random inputs is described. The approach is based on a frequency-domain second-order Volterra functional series representation for a dual-input/multiple-output system. The feasibility of the approach is demonstrated with the aid of a computer simulation for a known system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Anti-aliasing VLSI digital filters for video signal coders
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An antialiasing digital filter for video coders, meeting the CCIR Rec. 601 requirements for A/D (analog-to-digital) interfaces, is described. The input signal is oversampled at a frequency that is four times the nominal one; this cuts the complexity of the analog front end filter down to a simple RC stage. Furthermore the input resolution is reduced to 7 b as the eighth bit is recovered during the filtering and decimation phase. A dedicated methodology for the design of 1-D high-speed FIR filters has been developed; it includes programs for filter synthesis and optimization, for the simulation of the processing effects on a video signal, and for a semiautomatic conversion of the final circuit into a CMOS application-specific IC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of high-frequency active RC-filters using passive compensation methods
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Versatile methods for passive compensation of nonideal operational amplifiers used in high-frequency active RC-filters are presented. Two main filter building blocks, inverting and noninverting integrators, are made ideal for amplifiers having a single pole gain roll-off using an additional resistor for each integrator. The methods are applicable to all integrator-based filters, such as biquads and ladder filters, as well as some single amplifier biquads. Computer simulations and experimental results confirm the theories. An elliptic bandpass filter is considered as a design example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of an L-band monolithic GaAs receiver front-end with low power consumption
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Design aspects of a broadband GaAs monolithic receiver circuit operating at L-band are discussed. The circuit consists of a low-noise amplifier, buffer amplifier, and mixer. Various measures taken to minimize the DC-power consumption are described. Operation with less than 100 mW has been simulated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An accurate and efficient multiple delay simulator for MOS logic circuits using polynomial approximation
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A technique is proposed for the multiple delay simulation of NMOS and CMOS logic circuits. For the simple inverter the rise or fall delay time is approximated by a product of polynomials of the input waveform slope, the output loading capacitance, and the device configuration ratio, with the polynomial coefficients so determined as to best fit the SPICE simulation results for a given fabrication process. This approach can easily be extended to the case of multiple input transitions. The simulation results show that the proposed method can predict the delay times within 5% error and with a speedup of a factor of three orders of magnitude for several circuits tested, as compared with the SPICE simulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of adaptive filters
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The adaptive filter design and implementation (AFDI) interactive software package is a set of programs for design, evaluation, and implementation of adaptive filters. AFDI includes adaptive filters, signal generation, data acquisition, file management, signal analysis, and TMS32010 assembly code generation facilities. AFDI allows repeated evaluation of the performance of a filter to select optimum structure, algorithm, and parameter values for particular applications. Many routines that provide rudimentary capabilities for constructing adaptive filters are included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Linear frequency networks with applications to 'frequency set-on' oscillators
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A linear frequency network is a network system which consists of an arbitrary connection of devices, each of which perform a linear transformation on the instantaneous frequency of a signal. Thus, a transfer function may be defined relating the output to input instantaneous frequency. Particular networks are investigated, including a basic section, producing a self-adaptive bandpass filter which is then applied to a frequency set-on oscillator. Such an oscillator is a multimode oscillator where any mode will be stable when excited by a sample of an RF pulse adjacent to the mode. Experimental devices in the 400-600-MHz band are shown to have excellent agreement with theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: From algorithm conception to product manufacture: an automated design approach
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe a fully integrated design environment geared toward the mapping of algorithms to application-specific integrated circuits. This design environment consists of a family of silicon compilers, each of which is geared toward a specific architecture, implemented using a well-structured software environment (FACE). The system description language and compilation tools associated with this methodology allow the designer to work at the conceptual and architectural level while being sheltered from the need to craft details at the device and circuit level. A detailed design example describes this methodology, emphasizing the reduction in design time and manpower required. The results of chip designs using this design approach are also highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the design of maximally flat nonrecursive digital bandpass and bandstop filters
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A method is presented for designing maximally flat nonrecursive digital (MFNRD) bandpass and bandstop filters with specified center frequency, bandwidth, and transition bandwidth. It permits direct computation of the filter coefficients and is based on the transformation of prototype MFNRD low- and high-pass filters. A FORTRAN program has been developed for the method described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On routing and performance comparison of techniques for packet-switched networks using learning automata
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Distributed adaptive routing algorithms with the ability to adaptively proportion traffic over several paths is proposed for packet-switched data networks. A learning automaton is situated at each node of the network where a routing decision must be made and directs traffic entering the node onto one of the outgoing links. Using network feedback, and automaton modifies its routing strategy to improve its link selections. This approach has the advantage over existing routing schemes of offering a simple and extremely practical feedback and updating policy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear matched filtering and neural networks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A class of nonlinear matched filters is discussed. These filters involve the transformation of the signal spectrum and the filter transfer function through a nonlinearity, before they are multiplied in the transform domain. The resulting filter structures are equivalent to three-layer neural nets. They have better performance in terms of signal discrimination than previously known filters. The matched filters are further subdivided into two major classes according to the DFT (discrete Fourier transform) or the RDFT-based filtering. DFT and RDFT are approximations to the complex and real Fourier transforms, respectively. The RDFT-based filtering gives better performance in terms of spatial resolution, intermediate noise, and signal discrimination than the DFT-based filtering.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Long-term and short-term frequency stabilities in sinusoidal oscillators
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Deterministic considerations addressing linear sinusoidal oscillators are presented. The considerations are complex-frequency-domain ones and start with the fact that every oscillator can be represented as a closed loop of positive feedback. On the basis of such a model, a simple expression for variations in oscillation frequency omega /sub 0/ is developed. Since the model is a general, unified representation of various oscillators, it makes it possible to compare properties of circuits of different types and classes. Examples of RC oscillators with a passive feedback network and examples of active RC oscillators are discussed as particular cases of the general concept. Long-term changes in omega /sub 0/, are considered as variations under conditions of fixed oscillation amplitude, while short-term changes in this frequency are considered as variations under conditions of varying oscillation amplitude.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Area-efficient drawings of rectangular duals for VLSI floor-plan
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors consider the problem of finding the most area-efficient floorplan for macro cell (or general cell) layout, which satisfies all the constraints imposed not only on the area and the aspect ratio of each block but also on the length of the abutment between blocks. The floorplanning is implemented on the assumption that the relative position of each block has been specified in terms of a rectangular dual. The main task is composed of two algorithms; one is to find an area-efficient drawing of a rectangular dual D under these constraints, and the other is to estimate a lower bound to the area required to draw D. Using these algorithms together with the one to enumerate all rectangular duals, a floorplanning scheme is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An exhaustive generation of switched-capacitor circuits: a symbolic simulation and artificial intelligence approach
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors propose a mixed algorithmic-declarative method to solve a problem of structure generation. They demonstrate the usefulness of the declarative language PROLOG in comparison with classical procedural languages and show the importance of symbolic network simulators in this context. This method has been applied to practical problems in the domain of switched-capacitor circuits. SCYMBAL, a symbolic simulator for switched-capacitor circuits, has been used for that purpose. Results obtained in the case of the systematic generation of new integrator structures for high-frequency use are presented. The proposed method can be extended to different classes of analog circuits, for example, RC-filters, microwave circuits, and A/D converters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automated analysis of timing faults in synchronous MOS circuits
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The application of the SLOCOP timing verifier, which uses a rule-based subcircuit partitioning, is considered. The rule-based method is used to transform the network of MOS transistors, obtained from the physical layout by extraction into a network of unidirectional subcircuits. Each subcircuit is characterized by a logic model, which is used to accurately derive the timing constraints. The timing model of the circuit, required by this algorithm, is derived from the created subcircuit structure. The logic model makes it possible to eliminate false edges in the signal propagation graph. The resulting timing verifier can be used for a wide range of static and dynamic nMOS and CMOS circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Noise and sensitivity optimization of actively compensated active RC filters based on Friend-Deliyannis SAB
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The noise performance of two actively compensated second order active RC bandpass filters based on Friendly-Deliyannis single-amplifier biquads (SAB) has been evaluated. Design procedures for obtaining minimal noise as well as minimum sensitivity are also considered. Results are presented on two composite amplifier biquads.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Inductive inference of model structure using hypothesis feedback
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe initial results in the application of methods based on discrete decision theory to the inductive inference of models from collected data. The results are applied to the classification of electric distribution system customers for direct load control. These preliminary results are intended as an exploratory attempt to use discrete decision theory for inference of the structure of large collections of data. The analysis of collected data is modeled as a set of operations which induce equivalence relations on the data and generate meaningful figures of merit for the resulting equivalence classes. The effect is to reduce the data analysis problem to the detection of structure in the figure of merit functions over the set of equivalence classes. An inference algorithm is used to detect this structure and classify the customers into load types.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis of immittance function using current conveyors
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: General synthesis methods of immittance functions and immittance elements using second-generation current conveyors (CCIIs) are proposed. Immittance functions which consist of various immittance elements in series or in parallel can be simulated systematically by choosing the number of CCIIs and passive elements. Immittance elements which are proportional to the nth (n is an integer) power of complex angular frequency can be obtained. It is shown experimentally that the inductance simulator and the 2nd-order high-pass filter using a resistance-inductance parallel simulator work successfully.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of bit-serial recursive digital filters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A single-chip digital filter capable of realizing a single class of transfer function with programmable cutoff frequencies, stopband attenuation, and passband ripple has been designed and implemented. The filter is implemented using a pipelined bit-serial two's-complement arithmetic architecture. Six different recursive digital filter structures were analyzed to determine the minimum signal and coefficient wordlengths required to obtain the same performance with each of the filters. This information was then used to estimate the maximum sample rate possible and the number of gates that would be required to implement each filter structure using the same gate array fabrication technology. The bilinear LDI digital filter chosen for implementation required the least gates for an architecture in which on pipelined bit-serial multiplier is shared throughout the filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: McClellan transformation for two-dimensional IIR digital filter design
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The McClellan transformation is extended to the design of two-dimensional zero-phase and causal IIR (infinite impulse response) digital filters. In the case of a circularly symmetric contour, explicit conditions for a certain globally type preserving property are given, where the corresponding extended McClellan transformation is consequently of the so-called scaling-free form. Examples for circularly symmetric and elliptical contours are presented. A comparison with other McClellan transformations shows the advantages of the extended transformation for the approximation of a given contour.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Detection of damper winding currents and the damping coefficient of a synchronous machine using a predictor corrector estimator
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors propose a nonlinear estimator for detecting instantaneous state and determining up-to-date parameters of a synchronous generator. Simulation results illustrate the performance of this predictor corrector estimator (PCE) with different weighting matrices. With a proper choice of the weighting matrix Q, the PCE gives excellent results, converging globally.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Architecture of a new ASIC data communication circuit intended for the ISO levels 3, 4, 5: network, transport and session
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The functional specification and the architecture of the MC3 chip are described. Specific advanced aspects of this work concern at first the main target: a novel application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) data communication circuit intended for the high-level ISO protocols network, transport, and session. Secondly, they concern the functional requirements of the target circuit: it must run each announced level or a subset of the 3 levels; with each hypothesis are given an upper bound for the number of authorized connections, and a lower bound for the corresponding throughput. Emphasis is placed on the definition of the MC3 chip architecture, its external interface and the embedded systems architecture in which the chip will operate. It is also shown how the validation of the whole defined architecture is carried out: by implementing a high-level simulation on a multi-Transputer-based machine and by logical simulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accurate modeling and simulation of parallel interconnection in high-speed integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The evaluation of the time-domain performance of interconnection lines is becoming increasingly more important in the analysis and design of high-speed integrated circuits. An accurate computer model for n coupled microstrip lines is developed for circuit simulation. Modal analysis is applied to decouple the n coupled line system into n independent lines and the characteristic solution of the lossy transmission line equation is modeled into a simple time-varying equivalent circuit. This model has been implemented into a circuit simulator, called iSMILE, that significantly reduces the model development time. Simulation results on propagation delay times and crosstalks are presented for the case of high-speed GaAs HEMT (high-electron-mobility transistor) integrated circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The role of participation factors in reduced order eigenanalysis of large power systems
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present a family of variable transformations which are aimed at improving the performance of selective modal analysis (SMA) algorithms. The value of such transformations has been assessed with participation factors and participation ratios. These transformations are applied at two subsystem levels: generator and area level. It is shown that their successive application allows an important order reduction while maintaining convergence of SMA algorithms. Emphasis is on a specific feature of a family of simple and physically meaningful variable transformations: the feasibility of accumulating the participation of the modes of interest on a few state variables.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parallel processing scheme for tree-structured image generation system
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A parallel ray tracing scheme has been implemented on a loosely coupled multimicrocomputer system. Improvements are made by extending the architecture from a star structure to a hierarchical tree structure. This makes it possible to generate animated images at higher speed. The authors outline a hierarchical tree-structured image-generation system and discuss the parallel processing mechanisms of data transfer and hierarchical load distribution schemes. Problems with the tree-structured system are pointed out, and remedies are examined (area redistribution, and adaptive subdivision). Experiments are carried out to evaluate the performance of the tree-structured system in image generation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear C-filters for nonstationary signals and deconvolution in impulsive noise
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The combination filter or C-filter incorporates both temporal and rank-order information of the input sequence to produce its outputs. It can be used as an equalization filter to restore an original waveform which has been dispersed by a channel, in the presence of additive white Gaussian and impulsive noise. The filter coefficients can be designed by using the LMS (least mean squares) algorithm. This approach is examined and an example is given demonstrating the usefulness of the C-filter. The authors consider a technique which combines both rank-order statistics and FIR (finite impulse response) filtering schemes to deconvolve noisy channel characteristics, and to simultaneously reject the impulse noise. The problem of gain normalization at frequencies other than zero is also addressed; this arises during filtering of nonstationary signals in impulsive noise. It is concluded that the C-filter provides a useful alternative to the FIR filter for applications in inverse filtering and frequency-selective nonstationary signal restoration when the additive noise contains impulsive components and step nonstationarity in signal level.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transient analysis of DC to DC converters in discontinuous operation mode by using alternator equations
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The time-varying part of a power electronic circuit formed by two switching elements is extracted in a two-port called an alternor. The V-I constitutive equations of the alternor are defined and depend on two time-varying parameters, alpha and beta . The remaining part of the network is linear time-invariant. The modified nodal equations of the cyclically switching circuit are formulated by including the alternor equations. The s-domain solution holds for all transients of the circuit. Its inverse Laplace transform represents the global time-domain response, which, particularized for the corresponding values of alpha and beta in each switched interval, gives the partial analytic solutions of the converter for each switched configuration. By using these expressions cyclically, together with boundary and threshold conditions, a computer program can give the transient and steady-state response.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Finding multiple solutions of piecewise-affine resistive circuits
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A combinatorial method for finding all solutions of piecewise-affine resistive circuits is presented. The method is applied to a proposed representation of piecewise-affine equations which uses convex-set theory, but in no way is it restricted to this representation. Based on the developed method, a systematic search scheme is given to determine the regions which have solutions including infinite ones, and its efficiency is compared to other combinatorial methods given in the literature. It is noted that the proposed method does not necessitate the calculation and the existence of the inverse of the Jacobian matrix in any region. Thus, it is capable of finding infinite solutions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bit level processor arrays: current architectures and a design and programming tool
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors review bit-level processor arrays and the common characteristics that make them ideal for VLSI and high-speed computations. Emphasis is on arrays that have been implemented rather than proposed architectures. The essential features shared by these arrays, and those that differentiate them are characterized and used to develop a taxonomy for bit-level processor arrays. The authors also discuss programming tools, with an emphasis on RAB, a large program used to map a class of algorithms written in C onto bit-level processor arrays. The basic components and extensions to RAB are discussed. Directions of current research and design of bit-level processor array architectures and their programming environments are also briefly discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis of speed-independent circuits from algebraic specifications
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors propose a novel method for the synthesis of asynchronous speed-independent circuits that communicate using handshaking protocols. The circuit's behavior is specified through a collection of properties. Each property is expressed algebraically and describes a partial view of the required behavior. The global behavior is obtained by the Boolean product of the algebraic expressions. Classical techniques of race-free synthesis are then adapted to take into account external environments (users) which do not necessarily respect the fundamental mode hypothesis. The method is illustrated by a dual-rail code queue element that communicates using a four-cycle signaling protocol on both the input-data and the output-data interconnections.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new combined time-delay adaptive filter
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The proposed combined time-delay adaptive filter combines some advantages possessed by common types of the FIR (finite-impulse response) adaptive filter. These advantages include its simple configuration, its covering a long period of signal response, as well as a fast convergence speed. In addition, this adaptive filter is more suitable for the baseband full-duplex two-wire data transmission system, particularly in the ISDN (integrated-service digital network) U-interface subscriber loop, as an echo canceller. In implementation, the architecture is mainly based on a digital signal processor chip.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of digital signal transmission channels on coronating power lines
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A procedure is presented to evaluate transient responses of multiconductor power line carrier channels to any input digital signal code. The method involves the synthesis of an autoregressive filter to simulate corona noise on HV transmission lines. An accurate model of the multiconductor power line and a rigorous propagation algorithm are used. The single-phase and two-phase couplings most suitable for digital transmission on a practical three-phase line are selected. Transmission capacity limits for various lengths and different signal-to-corona noise ratios are given. Results of an extensive series of simulation tests run on a practical 380-kV power line are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A VLSI systolic filter with ternary coefficients for delta-modulated signals
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The realization of a digital FIR (finite impulse response) filter for both input data and coefficients encoded with ternary levels by delta-sigma modulation (DSM) is described. Due to the ternary values, multibit calculations are not needed. The filter architecture is very regular, highly parallel, and pipelines. The filter is easily made adaptive, as coefficients can be changed during normal operation. It is composed of bit-level systolic arrays whose cells are designed to allow a working frequency and consequently a throughput rate close to the limit of the technology used. A filter with 160 taps was realized in a 3- mu m H-CMOS technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A testable CMOS signal processor for fast Fourier transforms
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present the architecture of a fast Fourier transform processor which has high performance characteristics and an embedded test structure that allows the processor to test itself during normal operation. The properties of separable residue codes have been used for error detection in the arithmetic unit of the processor. Offline error detection which tests for the classic stuck at faults is based on the properties of the dynamic CMOS logic design used. The testing circuitry used in the architecture accounts for only a 20% area overhead and no time ahead, an important saving in a signal-processing environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new echo canceller realized by high performance digital signal processor
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A multi-echo-path echo canceller (MEP-EC) is described, which works well together with a microphone selection unit. Echo cancellation performance was measured in a teleconference room, and 28-dB echo cancellation was obtained. The echo cancellers were implemented in an acoustic echo canceller system, ACII, for teleconferencing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A unified mixed-mode digital/analog simulation environment
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A unified mixed-mode digital/analog simulator called Lsim is described, which combines a behavioral multidelay simulator, an RC-switch level simulator, circuit simulation based on the ADEPT algorithm, and circuit simulation based on direct solution to be used on analog circuits. The different simulation algorithms are combined into a single, consistent, unified simulation environment. Each algorithm is described, as well as the interaction between them when mixed-mode simulation is performed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Waveform relaxation applied to transient device simulation
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors investigate the possibility of accelerating the transient simulation of MOS devices by using waveform relaxation. Standard spatial discretization techniques are used to generate a large, sparsely-connected system of algebraic and ordinary differential equations in time. The waveform relaxation algorithm for solving such a system is described, and several theoretical results that characterize its convergence for device simulation are given. One-dimensional experimental results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Statistical MOS VLSI circuit optimization with non-nested experimental design
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present an efficient method that minimizes the circuit performance sensitivities to the MOSFET parameter fluctuations. A worst-case and squared-error loss function is used to evaluate the noise sensitivity of a design. The statistical circuit performance is modeled as a function of both the transistor channel widths and a noise parameter, and circuit simulation points are selected by an experimental design strategy that assumes no experimental errors. The fitted performance model is then used to predict and optimize the worst-case performance and the squared-error loss function. Compared with the method of G. Taguchi and Y. Wu (1985) in two circuit examples, the proposed method requires about 60% fewer circuit simulations and predicts the loss functions with comparable or better accuracy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computationally efficient determination of threshold voltages in narrow-channel and short-channel MOSFETs using infinite-network manipulations
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Infinite network theory provides a computationally advantageous method for computing the threshold voltage of a narrow-channel or short-channel MOSFET. It takes into account the fringing of the electric field upward into the air and sideways into the oxide and semiconductor. This approach also has the advantages of smaller computer memory requirements and execution times as compared with the classical method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systematic design of systolic arrays using mapping algorithm
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method to derive the architecture of systolic arrays is discussed. The focus is on the mapping algorithm proposed by D.I. Moldovan (Proc. IEEE, vol.71, no.1, p.113-20, 1983). The algorithm is based on the idea of transforming the indices of the do-loop structured program into time and space using a matrix. It is shown that many requirements which appear in the practical design of the systolic array can be expressed by the mathematical constraints of the matrix. These constraints allow a more systematic determination of the transformation matrix.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic multilayer routing for surface mounted technology
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present an automatic routing procedure for multilayer technology, especially surface-mounted devices. The problem is to perform a wiring in a minimum number of routing layers. The pads to be connected are rectangular regions on the top layer. A channel model has been developed in which routing layers are arbitrarily divided into horizontal and vertical (HV) channels containing pads within the channel area. They may also contain areas blocked with wiring. The method is composed of global and final routing, performing a modified HV routing, allowing jogs within every layer. Global routing is based on a graph-theoretical model. Final routing then becomes an assignment problem and is solved by a cut-strategy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach for circuit extraction based on overlay graph
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Presents an approach for circuit extraction that considers the physical significance of each overlay in multilayer IC masks. The overlay graph transformed from mask artwork data keeps the topological and geometric information of integrated circuits. The extraction based on the overlay graph implements a transformation from an IC chip layout to a circuit representation suitable for detailed circuit simulation. The approach can be applied to MOS and bipolar IC technologies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Linear algorithms for computing closed loop polynomials of 2-D systems
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Some problems connected with the construction of 2-D compensators and observers are analyzed. In particular, the authors consider algebraic criteria and linear algorithms for selecting 2-D stable polynomials which can be realized as closed-loop characteristic polynomials of a 2-D system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: VLSI signal generation in echo canceler transceiver
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A pulse-shaper and convolver system suitable for a 2B1Q echo-canceler transceiver is presented. A very flexible, reproducible and testable digital circuit with 70-80-dB accuracy and linearity can be produced inexpensively in VLSI. Breadboard performance meets ISDN (integrated-services digital network) U-interface specifications. The approach has the flexibility to synthesize other baseband signals like 4B3T and 3B2T.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Readout of IR detector arrays below LHe temperatures
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The readout electronics of the telescope cameras aboard the European Infrared Space Observatory will have to be operated at temperatures of about 2-4 K. To develop a suitable CMOS process, the authors studied the influence of different technological parameters on cryogenic device behavior. On the basis of research on cryogenic CMOS processing, they developed a design approach for the readout circuitry of the far-infrared photometric camera required for the ISOPHOT experiment. Since long time drifts of device characteristics due to cosmic ionizing radiation have to be considered, they propose a concept based on differential double sampling and detection of soft errors by nondestructive readout.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new average model of switching converters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The state-space average model is extended to multitopology switching-mode DC-DC converters and modified to have high precision without increased computation. The modified model is used both in continuous-conduction-mode (CCM) and discontinuous-conduction-mode (DCM) switching DC-DC converters. In particular, the modified model can be used for small-signal analysis of switching-mode PWM DC-DC converters, especially in computer-aided analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi-fault diagnosis of DC-nonlinear analog circuits
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A method for the fault diagnosis of DC nonlinear analog circuits is proposed. The concepts of independent faulty node compensating current and fault component are introduced, and the sufficient and necessary condition for testability is stated. It is shown that nonlinear networks can be diagnosed effectively if all the nonlinear elements are accessible and there are certain linear accessible nodes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New trends in circuit design via expert system
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The architecture of a tool for synthesizing electrical networks by using an expert system is outlined. The advantages of the method are discussed in comparison with traditional ones. The steps through which the method develops are illustrated, and a sketch of a knowledge base implemented for power-supply circuit synthesis is reported together with a synthesis example. The method has been implemented successfully for the synthesis of DC power supply networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of a symmetrical diplexer composed of canonical Butterworth two-port networks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors study the design of a diplexer composed of two canonical Butterworth two-port networks having low-pass and high-pass characteristics. The problem can be simplified to that of choosing the order of the Butterworth response and determining the cutoff frequencies of the Butterworth two-port networks. To obtain a symmetrical diplexer characteristic, it is shown that the cutoff frequency of the low-pass two-port network and that of the high-pass two-port network should be chosen symmetrically with respect to the crossover frequency. A computer program, DIPLX, that gives the required results as well as the frequency response of the transducer power-gain characteristics was used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Net assignment in gate matrix layout
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In the gate matrix layout approach for CMOS circuits, columns are first rearranged so as to minimize the number of rows needed. This problem is known to be NP-hard. When this is completed, the sets of nets and vertical diffusion runs are determined. The next problem is to assign the nets to rows so that the gate matrix can by physically laid out with minimum area. It is shown that this problem is also NP-hard and a heuristic algorithm is proposed for this problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient structure for nonlinear L- and C-filtering
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a pipelined structure for real-time L- and C-filtering operations which uses a number of pipeline stages less than or equal to the number of bits in the binary representation of the input data. The method uses a bit-level thresholding operation on input data in binary representation and distributed arithmetic.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A circuit simulator based on the waveform-relaxation method using selective overlapped partition and classified latencies
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Several techniques for improving simulation costs in the waveform relaxation method are discussed. In the circuit partitioner field, selective overlapped partition and duplication depth ideas are proposed. For the circuit simulation part, several modifications to the conventional simulator are demonstrated and classified latencies proposed. Experimental simulations are compared with results obtained from SPICE2. The results indicate conclusively that, if the circuit size is over one thousand, SUPER-SPICE is more cost-effective than SPICE2.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of DSP applications using the AT&T DSP32 C compiler and application library
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors briefly introduce the C compiler and the application library for the DSP32 digital signal processor (DSP). Several examples are shown that illustrate the ease of writing C programs for some common filtering applications. In most cases, a small real-time penalty is incurred by using C, rather than assembly language coding. Programming in C, however, allows a dramatic improvement in programmer productivity in terms of implementing, testing, and maintaining an application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Elimination of transients in LPC based vocoders
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: It is known that transient impulses will appear in LPC (linear predictive coding)-based speech coders and vocoders because the filter parameters are changed periodically while an input signal is applied. These impulses may be heard as clicks and may cause overflow in electronic circuits. It is shown that the transients may be eliminated by changing the state vector appropriately at the same time as the filter parameters are changed. Expressions are derived for calculating such a change, and the validity of the proposed approach is demonstrated by simulations of a pitch-excited vocoder. Complete elimination of transients is achieved. Different filter structures behave differently with regard to transients, but it is shown that there are pair of states in two filters that will cause the same transients when the transfer functions are identical but the structures differ.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel approach for high-frequency pipelined A/D conversion
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Flash and parallel approaches are compared with the pipeline solution, and the advantages of the latter technique are evaluated. A pipeline design is examined extensively, and circuit improvements suitable for increasing conversion speed are described. The proposed scheme includes a self-calibration to compensate conversion errors, in particular the error resulting from the use of very fast op-amps with low DC gain. A novel approach for speeding up the pipeline converter, referred to as digital assisted slewing is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new scheme for the Steiner problem in graphs
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The Steiner problem in graphs has found important application in global and detailed routeing of integrated circuit layout. A scheme is described which does not immediately construct a tree, but first obtains an initial tree, and then concentrates on refining it. A loop method for refining is presented, and an algorithm is developed. The algorithm is of low time and space complexity, and experimental results show that it performs well.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive nonlinear image restoration using the theory of convex projections
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An adaptive, nonlinear restoration algorithm incorporating both regularization and ringing suppression constraints is developed. The algorithm is formulated using the method of projections onto convex sets. In the proposed method, regularized restoration is implemented by projecting at each iteration onto the extended Wiener set. Ringing suppression is achieved by adaptively bounding the regional image variance in an attempt to reduce the energy of the ringing artifacts.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of an array processing unit for an array processor
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An effort was made to design a small and cheap array processing unit (APU) to be used in a major distributed process array processor system for digital signal-processing applications. From the task definition and environment analysis, a design is presented. The unit, based on the Texas TMS 32020 and Intel 80186 is of the load-and-forget type and provides efficient memory management and operand accessing techniques to speed up the processing. An example is provided to illustrate details of the implementation and performance. It is concluded that the design presented fulfils requirements outlined for the APU.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimal varying dyadic structure models of time invariant systems
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The problem of approximation of a time-invariant system by a varying dyadic structure model is considered. The increase in network implementation complexity of varying structure systems is avoided by considering dyadic groups only. The problem of best approximation in Euclidean norm is solved, and it is shown that, in general, there does not exist a one-to-one correspondence between causal and symmetric linear systems and their best models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On a new CMOS resistor implementation for linear analog IC signal processing applications
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A CMOS implementation of a linearized floating resistance is presented, in which the resistor value depends only on the beta of a matched set of NMOS transistors, and on a bias current I/sub B/. A linear amplifier is realized by combining two resistors and one op amp. In this circuit the nonlinearities of the individual resistors cancel; fully differential operation is not required. Experimental data show good agreement with simulation results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimization of circuits by sampling in solid angle segments bordered by ellipsoids
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A statistical Monte Carlo-based procedure for the optimization of the performance of a given electrical circuit is introduced. In the proposed strategy, the total cloud of points in the parameter space generated by a Monte Carlo analysis is approximated by sampling only in a few selected solid angles bordered by hyperellipsoids. As this saves a considerable amount of CPU time, additional search procedures could be introduced that avoid local optima even in cases where other statistical methods fail. The effectiveness of the algorithm is demonstrated by two examples: a bipolar amplifier and a noninverting NMOS superbuffer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Qualitative analysis of neural networks
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The stability properties of a given equilibrium point of a neural network are determined. Given that a specific equilibrium point of a neural network is asymptotically stable, an estimate for its domain of attraction is established. Finally, given a set of initial conditions and external inputs, estimates for corresponding trajectory bounds are established.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis of nonreciprocal 2-D filters
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A method for designing nonreciprocal 2-D filters is proposed. The approach is based on the use of nonreciprocal one-way lines and 1-D reciprocal subnetworks. The problem of the approximation and realization of 2-D filters can then be solved in terms of the 1-D filter theory. Two examples are considered: a mixed lumped-distributed network and a wave-digital filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A unified formulation technique for the analysis of periodically switched networks
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A general and systematic formulation technique is proposed for the analysis of periodically switching networks containing resistors, inductors, capacitors, independent voltage sources, voltage-controlled voltage sources, and switches. As a result, both switched-capacitor networks and switched DC-DC converters can be handled by the proposed method. The resultant formulation is a novel type of modified nodal approach in which the number of circuit variables is effectively reduced and no zero-diagonal entries would, in general, appear in its matrix.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A perfect interpolation of discrete Fourier transform
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors consider conditions and a solution for a perfect interpolation of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) spectrum. Free variables in the problem are chosen to enable the shortest sequence length. Some sequences for an efficient implementation in cascade interpolation structures are computed, and the required number of multiplications for the procedure is determined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new CMOS circuit representation for timing verification
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A structured logical circuit expression (SLICE) is proposed to unify the representation of restoring logic gate and path transistor logic, which are two major logic styles in CMOS circuit design. The SLICE representation provides a systematic way to describe signal flow in CMOS transistor networks. Timing verification can be easily performed by the SLICE representation due to its natural capacity for path enumeration and critical path analysis. Moreover, signal paths and logic stages of a CMOS circuit can be identified to facilitate efficient timing verification.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The computation of positive definite solutions to the 2-D Lyapunov equation via a matrix Riccati equation
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Two algorithms for computing positive definite solutions to the 2-D Lyapunov equation are presented, based on the discrete-time strictly-bounded-real lemma. These algorithms require the solution of a matrix Riccati equation and are based on the algebraic solution of the spectral factorization problem. The problem of solving the 2-D Lyapunov equation is reduced to solving a series of 1-D problems. Examples illustrate the proposed algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rectilinear drawing of a graph on a plane with the minimum number of line segments
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A riveted graph G(V,E) is a graph whose vertices are fixed on a plane. Its rectilinear drawing D(G) is a configuration of G on the plane in such a way that every edge is composed of horizontal and vertical line segments. The authors consider the problem of reducing the number of line segments and present an algorithm to obtain such a rectilinear drawing that the total number of line segments is no more than 3 mod E mod . It is noted that a drawing so obtained contains no edge composed of five line segments. The algorithm runs in O( mod E mod ) time and space.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A generalized technique for the synthesis of 2-D state-space digital filters with minimum roundoff noise
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A generalized technique has been developed for the synthesis of 2-D state-space filter structures which minimize the roundoff noise under a scaling constraint. This is based on the Fornasini-Marchesini local-state-space (LSS) model. The optimal filter structure is found using a 2-D similarity transformation characterized by a nonsingular matrix which is not block-diagonal, but general. This allows one to synthesize the optimal filter structure by solving only one optimization problem. If some constraints are imposed on the Fornasini-Marchesini LSS model and the 2-D similarity transformation matrix, it is possible to easily arrive at the results based on the Roesser LSS model. The proposed theory is therefore quite general and simple.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Minimum sensitivity structure of 2-D digital filters based on the Fornasini-Marchesini model
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors treat the balanced realization and minimum sensitivity structure of two-dimensional (2-D) recursive digital filters. This structure is based on the Fornasini-Marchesini local state-space model. First, a technique is introduced for the balanced realization of 2-D recursive digital filters. Next, the sensitivities of a 2-D transfer function are investigated with respect to coefficients of the local state-space model. The overall sensitivity is then evaluated using the 2-D controllability and observability Gramians. It is also shown that the minimum sensitivity structure is easily derived from the balanced realization and under an l/sub 2/ scaling constraint it is equivalent to that with minimum roundoff noise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel approach to CAD of analog cells
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel approach is described which allows the user to generate analog integrated circuits in both CMOS and bipolar technology in a very efficient way. The system supports the design of analog circuits from scratch down to the final layout in an appropriate interchange format. The user will be guided through the design process, always being able to interrupt it. The design process thus becomes highly interactive, user friendly, and rapid. The only tools used within this system are simulators like SPICE, BONSAI, and DOSCA.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of the variance function for edge enhancement in multidimensional data
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A multidimensional variance function filter is defined and its performance in edge enhancement applications is evaluated. For the case of a 3*3 window, the variance filter is shown to perform comparably to the Sobel filter and better than the compass gradient filter. The advantage of the variance filter is its easy extendability to large window sizes and high dimensionality. The 3D variance filter is applied to the ventricular edge detection problem in gated nuclear cardiac imaging.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signal delay in distributed RC tree networks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors examine signal delay associated with distributed RC tree networks, and present an algorithm for computing distributed RC time constants. Skew measurements from a bipolar test chip utilizing various flip-flop loading configurations were used. The computer implementation of the algorithm used to check clock skew limits on a large bipolar ECL (emitter-coupled logic) gate array is also presented. On-chip clock skew, metal delays, and hold time margins are being analyzed and managed with this algorithm. The algorithm was implemented as an integral part of Tandem's CAD-based VLSI physical design system and is part of the system-wide clock skew management methodology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability evaluation as part of computer-aided power distribution network design
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A computer-aided method for the quantitative reliability analysis of medium-voltage distribution networks is developed. Using the data included in the network database, together with the reliability data for network components and the per-unit values for the energy not supplied, the outage rates, durations and costs can be evaluated. Using the reliability calculation program together with the other design programs, the optimal development plans for each network can be found. Both the technical restrictions and the total costs, including the costs of investments, losses and outages must be included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stability analysis of linear active circuit containing periodically switched resistors
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The problem of the stability analysis of linear active circuits containing periodically switched resistors (R-switched circuits) is considered. The state-space method, the classical theory of linear periodic systems of differential equations, and the Hurwitz stability criterion are used for stability analysis. From the analysis of simple examples of R-switched circuits it follows that linear models of such circuit transfer functions corresponding to the time intervals of constant resistance of switched resistors have poles which are located strictly in the left half-plane of the complex plane. As an example, the stability of the second-order circuit is investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An active RC filter capable of easy lowpass-highpass transformation
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An RC active filter, whose transfer characteristics can easily be changed from a given lowpass to its highpass form only by interchanging one capacitor and one resistor regardless of the order of the filter, is proposed. The transfer function realizable by this method are limited to odd-order Butterworth and a class of elliptic functions which have their poles on a circle in the complex s-plane. A novel all-pass active RC structure, which has the transfer level of 1.0 independent of the quality factor of the transfer function and is quite suitable for the proposed realization, is also given. The experimental results on the fifth-order Butterworth filter show quite good agreement with theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of the large-signal behaviour of active filters
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A describing function representation of the saturation nonlinearity of operational amplifiers is used to formulate the nonlinear transfer functions of multiple-amplifier filters. The efficacy of various functional approximations for shortening computer time is assessed. Computationally efficient means of predicting jump resonance and nonlinear oscillations are presented, based on the representation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical approach for signal delay in general distributed networks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors consider a general network with telegraph equations modelling distributed elements and having, additionally, nonlinear capacitors. A global asymptotic exponential stability of the solution is given. A simple computable upper bound of the delay time is given. Numerical examples illustrate the usefulness of the results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An experimental verification of thermal simulation by WATAND for a bipolar RF power transistor
