publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: WATAND is the University of Waterloo's interactive circuit simulation program for simulating the combined electrical and thermal behaviour of transistors. The authors report on a comparison between thermal mappings of bipolar RF power transistors obtained using WATAND simulation techniques on the one hand and using thermochromic liquid-crystal experimental techniques on the other. This comparison was carried out to test the accuracy of the WATAND modelling and simulation methods prior to using the simulation tool as a design aid in developing some ballasted RF devices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bounding the processing time of forward-chaining rule-based systems
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors propose an analytical method for evaluating the processing time of forward-chaining rule-based systems. An upper bound on the computations is presented. Numerical examples are presented which point out the importance of rule and data structures in the efficient implementation of rule-based systems. It is concluded that very similar rule-base implementations can have significantly different computational characteristics. Thus, careful analysis should be applied to an online rule-based system, such as the Voltage Control Expert System for which fast response is important.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault analysis and parameter identification in linear circuits in terms of topological matrices
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An approach based on the concept of pencils of n-matrices for the fault analysis of analog networks containing linear active and passive elements is given. Starting from pencils of n-matrices in case of single measurements, a purely algebraic necessary and sufficient condition is obtained in terms of banded block-Toeplitz matrices which have topological information. It is also indicated how this approach can be generalized to multiple measurement sets.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Testability conditions for two-dimensional bilateral arrays
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present different sets of testability conditions for two-dimensional bilateral arrays. Different conditions are established with respect to the dependency of the testing process on the signal flow. Each set of testability conditions establishes the controllability and observability of every test vector. These testability conditions are proved to be applicable under different processing models as related to the three inputs of each cell in the array. Complexity issues, such as number of test vectors and time units, are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a new structured adaptive SAW filter
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An electrostrictive SAW device developed at Stanford University can be electrically biased to vary induced field on the substrate. This device can thus do convolution of input signals with variable weights. The authors introduce the design of an adaptive filter based on the SAW device, derive the convergence property and misadjustment of the algorithm, and model the coupling problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis method for switched-capacitor FIR decimators and interpolators
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method is given for the systematic synthesis of FIR (finite-impulse-response) switched-capacitor decimation and interpolation filters that includes the derivation of an optimum clocking scheme. The latter allows the maximum possible settling times for the operational amplifiers (OAs), thus minimizing response errors associated with finite OA slew-rate and bandwidth. An example, in which the time allowed for OA settling in a published circuit is increased by considerable factors, is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EEG transitions in the learning process of simple tasks
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors describe experiments in which subjects' EEG (electroencephalogram) sequences were measured while engaged in a task in an ordinary laboratory without special electromagnetic shielding, to identify any dependence of the EEG transition process on differences in tasks, to identify features of the EEG which would be an index to the proficiency of the subject, and to obtain some correlation between the index and the task performance of the subject. Results of a calculation task and a manual pursuit tracking task are presented. In the case of the calculation task, the alpha-wave power was found to be increased in the learning process, while in the manual tracking task, the alpha-wave power showed little increase in the learning process. For the manual tracking tasks, a sort of correlation was found between the task performance and the alpha-wave power.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient linearization of broadband amplifiers with more than an octave bandwidth by adequate combining compensation technique and negative feedback
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: It is demonstrated that amplifiers with more than a decade bandwidth that have very low nonlinearity as well as low quiescent power and relatively high gain can be designed by combining the negative-feedback technique and the cascade-compensation technique. The potential of the design strategy is demonstrated in connection with the development of a three-stage amplifier with bipolar transistors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis and simulation of multiprocessor based packet switching systems
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The performance of a multiprocessor-based packet switch is predicted using an analytic model that computes the switch throughput. Packet lengths can be either constant or exponentially distributed. The time it takes to process an incoming (or outgoing) packet is also a random variable with a geometric or exponential distribution. The basic fabric for the implementation of the packet switch is a multiple-bus interconnection network with two levels of buses. Paths inside the node are established and maintained for the duration of the memory access, not only for the time required to transfer data. The arbitration is done on a priority basis. The model uses known expressions for the bandwidth of tightly-coupled multiprocessor systems, reducing the extra computations to the simple task of solving two simultaneous algebraic equations. Simulation runs were carried out to validate the accuracy of the approximations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Image-sequence compression on a 68020-based multi-processor system
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A 68020-based multiprocessor image processing system has been developed which is adaptable, flexible, extendable, modular, and fast. With the present four-processor system, it is possible to decode approximately 10 frames/s, where each frame contains 16384 pixels, using an image sequence compression algorithm developed by the authors. System components and operation are described along with present system performance; and areas for future improvements are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic synthesis system of sequential circuits
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors have developed an automatic synthesis system of synchronous sequential circuits that is able to draw logical circuit diagrams and represent logical equations by using only a state diagram or a state transition table. In particular, the operations of the system can be executed easily, using an interactive procedure and introducing the same form of a state diagram or a state transition table as the general representation of sequential circuits. The logical circuit diagrams that have been drawn by the system can be linked to the completed logical simulation system and printed circuit board system in the CAD (computer-aided design) computer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Compensation for amplifier finite bandwidth in the design of switched capacitor networks
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A method is described for analyzing general switched-capacitor networks with nonideal amplifiers. The finite bandwidths of the amplifiers distort the response of the network from the required response. It is shown that by readjusting the poles and zeros of the transfer function the required response can be accurately restored. In such cases, readjusting the clock frequency and/or the phase timing will enable the designer to obtain a final response which is very close to the desired one. The described optimization procedure ensures the stability of the designed network. Illustrative examples are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Can voltage security indices predict voltage collapse problems in large-scale power networks?
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors give the necessary conditions needed for voltage collapse indicators (VCIs) to predict voltage collapse phenomena in a power system. At least two VCIs are needed: one for the static mechanisms and the other for the dynamic mechanisms. It is found that VCIs cannot correctly predict an impending voltage collapse. What type of voltage collapse phenomena can be predicted by the VCIs depends on whether the VCIs monitor the steady-state operating point or the dynamic operating point.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High level control of security and optimizing functions
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A three-level approach to the security and optimization of a power system is suggested involving existing techniques such as the optimal power flow and optimizing switching, rule-based techniques (expert systems), and decision support systems. Based on a very comprehensive definition of the security problem, the functions of the various techniques are derived. Examples are given where expert systems or the interaction of the operator become indispensable. A graph-based approach is worked out in which the methods are integrated. Additional rules are given for the control of the scheme. Further experience is extractable from the models and methods used in the scheme, which still must be complemented by the experience of the system operator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A standard cell automated layout for a CMOS 50 MHz 8*8 bit pipelined parallel Dadda multiplier
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An 8*8 bit pipelined parallel multiplier which uses the Dadda scheme is presented. The multiplier has been implemented in a 3- mu m n-well CMOS process with two layers of metal using a standard cell automatic placement and routing program. The design uses a form of pipelined carry look-ahead adder in the final stage of summation, thus providing a significant contribution to the high performance of the multiplier. The design is expected to operate at a clock frequency of at least 50 MHz and has a flush time of seven clock cycles. The design illustrates a possible method of implementing an irregular architecture in VLSI using multiple levels of low-resistance, low-capacitance interconnect and automated layout techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis and design of nonideal switched capacitor networks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The theory for analysis of general periodically switched linear networks is described. It can be used for analysis and design of nonideal switched-capacitor circuits with linear imperfections such as switch resistances and finite gain-bandwidth products of operational amplifiers. In addition to frequency response, sensitivity of the response to changes in element values is determined. This is needed in evaluating the quality of circuit and in the design by optimization. The proposed theory computes the exact response without any theoretical approximation or restriction on circuit topology. The theories have been implemented in an interactive computer program called WATSNAP (Waterloo Switched Network Analysis Program). Several numerical examples are evaluated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hybrid adaptive control of linear systems by parallel processing and switched capacitor techniques
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The implementation of a direct adaptive control algorithm using parallel processing techniques is discussed. The controller presented is hybrid in nature (continuous time feedback and discrete time gain adjustment) and recursive least squares identification is implemented using a well-known algorithm based on the Givens rotation. The main feature of the proposed scheme is the fact that it is designed for implementation on systolic arrays (for parameter identification) and switched-capacitor technology (to implement the compensator with adjustable parameters). Adaptive identification can be performed by two identical systolic arrays which triangularize appropriate matrices by use of orthogonal operations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computation of domains of attraction in the state-space of second degree nonlinear circuits and systems
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A method is given which allows an easy and effective computation of domains of attraction for the solutions of a class of second-degree nonlinear and nonautonomous circuits and systems. Both locally and globally attracting domains can be determined in the state-space. The method yields much better results than those obtained using the classical method of quadratic Liapunov functions, as shown by some examples. Furthermore, the results yield interesting information about the actual solutions of the state equations considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Embedding interconnection nets in square lattices
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors model an interconnection net for a circuit by a random graph. This makes it possible to calculate the distribution of the interconnection lengths when the net is embedded in a two-dimensional square lattice. The embedding is optimal in the sense that the cliques of the net are placed together. The square lattice is used as a model of a gate array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Language oriented data structures and their applications to power system operation and training
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe a data preparation which closely imitates the hierarchical structures and objects present in a power system and applies operational terminology in abbreviated form. The meshed topological linkage is expressed by syntax and references assigned to objects. The main aim is to use the proposed description for the data supply of a stand-alone training simulator, capable of modeling any power system described in terms of a dictionary that is predefined in meaning.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive covariance-type internally symmetric algorithm for LS FIR filtering with linear phase
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The least-squares design of linear phase filters is approached from a novel perspective to take advantage of the symmetry which is intrinsic to the problem. The structure of the proposed filter is based on an adaptive covariance-type algorithm that results in a substantial reduction in computational complexity compared to other existing schemes. The algorithm requires 12.5 multiplications and 18.5 additions per time recursion with p being the order of the filter. A fast O(p) initialization scheme is also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generalized graph decomposition and its applications
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A graph-classification concept is introduced, which extends the notion of dense, medium, and sparse graphs and makes the classification a function of a preassigned real nonnegative number. Important properties of various classes of graphs are discussed. An algorithm for the harmonious decomposition of a graph is proposed that yields a minimum basic set of the graph and determines the available range of the real nonnegative number. Harmonious decomposition is considered in connection with the hybrid method of network analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A triple low-power voltage output video 8-bit CMOS DAC
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe a CMOS 8-bit triple DAC (digital-to-analog converter) dedicated to video applications. Its main features are low-power consumption at a high video sampling rate (290 mW when sampled at 27 MHz and with 75- Omega loads) and a low-glitch level. Each converter uses a 2/sup N/R technique and an efficient voltage output amplifier for 75- Omega external load. It has been fabricated with an experimental 2- mu m CMOS telecom process with a 250-AA gate oxide thickness, one metallization level, and two polysilicon levels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the differential operation circuit based on the switched capacitor circuit
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A circuit which operates by normalizing the difference between two input currents by their summation, called a differential operation circuit with current inputs, is developed using a switched-capacitor circuit technique. This circuit operates with a nonlinearity of 0.1% for the summation of input currents greater than 1 mu A because of the removal of the analog divider used in the conventional circuit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A CMOS subscriber line audio processing circuit including adaptive balance
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The design of a CMOS subscriber-line audio processing circuit including self-adaptive trans-hybrid balance has been described. Its transmission performance has been shown to exceed CCITT specifications with up to 12 dB of transmit gain and receive loss. This has been achieved using a single 5-V power supply while maintaining simple analog interfaces to a subscriber line interface circuit. This circuit will enable the design of programmable and flexible line cards, superior transmission performance over those realized with more conventional components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System identification through first and second order information from the periodogram
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The use of first- and second-order information in the characterization of linear systems is considered. Consideration is given to the case when this information is not available but some samples are given of a random process which are the result of filtering white noise through the system. The authors examine an approach which, starting from one estimate of the autocorrelation function, gives rise to an ARMA (autoregressive moving-average) model for the system considered. The derivation of the model is achieved from an optimization point of view.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stability analysis of three-dimensional state-space systems
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a novel approach for the stability analysis of three-dimensional state-space systems based on the two-dimensional Fornasini-Marchesini model. Some necessary and sufficient conditions for the stability of the systems are given in terms of the norms of state matrices. It is shown that it is efficient to test the instability of a system in accordance with the unstable state matrices. Particularly, if the state matrices can commute, it is convenient to verify the stability of a system by eigenvalues of the state matrices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Existence of unique solutions for multirate FIR filters based on Lagrange multipliers
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The Lagrange multiplier method is presented for the design of FIR (finite-impulse-response) digital filters for multirate applications. It is shown that under certain conditions, the optimal filter can be obtained as the solution to a linear system of equations which is related to a Vandermonde matrix. As Vandermonde matrices are always nonsingular, the existence and uniqueness of the optimal solution are guaranteed. As an example, optimal lowpass prototype filter for an FFT (fast Fourier transform) filter bank of 64 bandpass channels was designed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On complex-normalized reflection coefficients of a terminated lossless two-port network
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present three theorems on the relations among the complex-normalized reflection coefficients of a terminated lossless two-port network. It is noted that the results are useful in the solution of the compatible impedance problem and the broadband matching problem both in terms of the analytic theory and the real-frequency technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automated generation of multiprocessor arrays
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors introduce a design methodology to synthesize a multiprocessor system from an algorithmic description (AD) of the digital system. This is done by first defining multiprocessor arrays to realize segments of the AD. Then, the microarchitecture of each processor is realized. It is shown how to define the processor algorithm description for each processor and how a processor algorithm description can be realized. Specifically, the design methodology used in the AMPSS (automated multiprocessor synthesis system) of the University of Texas at Arlington is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer approach for nonlinear forced oscillators
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe a computer approach to solve the stationary oscillations produced in nonlinear forced oscillating circuit driven by several external signals. The technique described is essentially based on the combined concepts of Fourier analysis and the harmonic balance method. The authors treat complicated oscillations in which there exist many components of frequencies, such as free-running frequency, driving frequencies, their sum and difference frequencies, and their harmonics. One of the advantages of the technique is that it is possible to obtain the solutions in less computation time compared to common simulation techniques. Schottky-diode analysis is considered as an example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Tridiagonal state-space digital-filter structures
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A synthesis procedure for tridiagonal state-space structures is presented. The synthesis procedure yields structures using a reduced number of multipliers, which are free of zero-input and constant-input limit cycles. In addition, its output roundoff noise is minimized by optimizing some free parameters. A numerical example illustrating the synthesis procedure is provided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new technique for ARMA system modelling
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A technique for determining autoregressive moving-average (ARMA) model parameters based on the effective use of null space characterization of the autocovariance matrix of response data record, is proposed. Simulation results have shown this method to yield good estimates of the model parameters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A systolic algorithm for the fast computation of the connected components of a graph
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors consider the description of a systolic algorithm to solve the connected-component problem. It is executed in a ring topology with N processors, requiring O(Nlog N) time without regard to the graph's sparsity. The algorithm-partitioning issue is also addressed, indicating how to optimally map the computations into fixed-size rings or linear arrays. The proposed algorithm leads to simple processing elements, data addressing, and control. These points make the systolic array highly implementable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital implementation of a coherent CPM system for mobile radio
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe the digital implementation of a continuous-phase-modulation (CPM) signaling scheme for land mobile radio applications. The transmitted signal is optimized in terms of bandwidth efficiency by nonlinear filtering. In the coherent receiver, synchronization and detection are performed separately to reduce complexity and improve acquisition performance. The authors explain the principles of transmitter and receiver and give details on the implementation. It is noted that the demonstration system will be capable of transmitting data at 16 kb/s over the narrowband mobile radio channel with channel spacing of 20 kHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A digital FSK discriminator circuit
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A technique is proposed which allows accurate discrimination between two FSK keying tones. The technique is used to develop a digital discriminator for the 1200 baud signal generated by CCITT V23 type modems. Simulation of the proposed system has shown that under ideal conditions, the isochronous distortion observed at the output of this system can be reduced to less than 1%. Further tests which have been carried out on this discriminator circuit show that it is relatively robust and retains its excellent performance in more practical implementations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Algorithms to select optimum matched performance of programmable filters in telephone networks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Two algorithms are described for optimizing the coefficients of programmable filters in telephone networks. The two algorithms work with the LMS (least-mean-squares) algorithm to find an optimal set of coefficients of a programmable FIR (finite-impulse response) filter in meeting the different requirements worldwide. The algorithms were simulated and verified experimentally.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear systems and input-output representations
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Nonlinear and multidimensional extensions of earlier recent theorems by the author are considered. Those results concern the representation of linear operators defined on a set of locally integrable inputs. They establish (for the first time) the existence of impulse responses and associated integral representations as well as the convergence of a classical sum to an integral, in a general setting in which a certain continuity condition plays a central role. They also provide necessary and sufficient conditions for a causal linear operator to have a convolution representation with a continuous impulse-response function. In particular, a representation theorem for nonlinear input-output maps is given that yields, as a special case, Volterra-series representations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Charge bifurcation structure of a basic RC driven relaxation oscillator
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A very simple model of an RC-driven relaxation oscillator is considered. This model retains all the significant properties experimentally observed by many authors in actual circuits, but has the advantage of making it possible to obtain simple and meaningful results. The status of first-order and multiple locking is defined and properties of the sets of values of the bifurcation parameter giving rise to locking or to chaos are investigated. The uniqueness of the value of the parameter that gives rise to locking for fixed values of time lag and rotational number is proved. It is shown how this result can be extended to very general kinds of RC-driven oscillators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simplified block LMS algorithm
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A simplified version of the block least mean square (LMS) algorithm is proposed. Compared with the conventional block algorithms, the proposed algorithm possesses the following features: (1) it has a relatively simple configuration and is more flexible in the selection of the block length L: (2) it gives a much larger complexity ratio than that given by the conventional block algorithms: (3) it has a convergence behavior not inferior to its counterpart given by G.A. Clack et al. (1981); and (4) it has potential for use in real-time processing environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Solution of nonlinear equations in the synthesis of linear networks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A network-synthesis technique is presented which is based on the solution of the nonlinear equations resulting from coefficient-matching the network function of the desired network to the specified function. The systematic elimination of component variables from the equation set obtained in this way leads to a high-order polynomial in just one such component variable; the roots of this polynomial then include and provide through back substitution all component-set solutions to the synthesis problem. The proposed technique, which provides an alternative to the direct mathematical synthesis and optimization methods, has been successfully implemented using LISP.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mathematical modelling of electricity distribution systems with several voltage levels
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A mathematical model for the optimization of electricity distribution networks with several voltage levels is described. In the model the objective function includes all the costs of the system. A suitable optimization method is used to minimize the objective function considering the technical constraints. The model is based on a greenfield situation with no existing networks and it gives the optimal values for the number and sizes of equipment at each voltage level. All the costs of this optimal system are also given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stabilization of chaos-an algebraic theory
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Summary form only given. A general problem statement can be stated as follows: given a (nonlinear) plant p, the problem is to find a (nonlinear) compensator c so that the overall system s is 'good', in the sense that no chaotic motion can be generated. More specifically, let G be the set of all n-input n-output (nonlinear) operators, H be the subset of G in which no chaotic motion can be produced. Now the control problem can be stated more precisely as follows: given p epsilon G, find c epsilon G so that s epsilon H. The general problem is far too difficult to be solved. However, two general results can be presented. These results are in the form of two theorems which both depend on an important property that H can be characterized by systems in which almost periodical inputs produce almost periodical outputs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synchronization and chaos in a real discrete phase-locked loop
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Attempts an experimental verification of a certain model of the discrete phase-locked loop (DPLL), whose behavior is typical for a wide class of DPLLs with a positive-going zero-crossing detector. The theoretical model is described by a one-dimensional dynamical system (an endomorphism of the circle S/sup 1/). The model proved to agree well with the experimental system. In a wide range of parameters (amplitude and frequency of the input signal), the DPLL works as a frequency divider. Out of the phase-locked region, the loop is not globally stable and a stable periodic oscillation with very long period appeared together with chaotic oscillations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gain-bandwidth restrictions for FET amplifiers with parasitic drain-to-gate coupling
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Analytic gain-bandwidth theory for solid-state microwave-frequency amplifiers has been developed only under the assumption of a very crude modeling of the active device (e.g. an FET), i.e. a voltage-controlled current source loaded by two capacitors at the input and the output ports. It is well known that a realistic model includes many more passive elements, including which resistors to take losses into account. The authors have derived gain bandwidth restrictions for a FET amplifier equalized at both ends, under the assumption that the FET is modeled as a transconductance loaded by gate, drain and gate-to-drain parasitic capacitances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Weighted random pattern testing based on test counts
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present an algorithm to generate weighted random test patterns based on multiple probability distributions. The algorithm to generate distributions is based on S.B. Akers and B. Krishnamurthy's test counting method, and has a running time which is linear in the number of gates. The algorithm has been implemented in C, and tested on several of the ISCAS benchmark circuits. The results are significantly superior to both pure random testing, and the weighted random pattern testing reported by R. Lisanke et al. (1986, 1987).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A DSP breath sound analyser
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The growing availability of powerful digital signal processors (DSPs) makes possible the real-time analysis of almost all common biological signals. The authors consider the spectral analysis of breath sounds, which may provide an objective and quantitative assessment of the respiratory pathology in patients with pulmonary disorders. The authors propose a breath-sound analyzer consisting of a pick-up accelerometer, a real-time FFT (fast Fourier transform) analyzer, and an interface with a general-purpose personal computer. The spectra of normal and pathological breath sounds were analyzed for validation of the apparatus.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modular multiprocessor system and its application to real-time speech coding
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Many multiple-digital-signal-processor (DSP) systems are not flexible enough to incorporate both additional tasks and new DSP elements. A possible philosophy for a universal' system without these drawbacks is developed. Basic tasks are defined very generally. They are mapped on general basic system elements: processing units, communication channels, processing control, and real-time interfaces. The restrictions for the actual implementation of each element are reduced to the necessary minimum, i.e. a communication standard. A realized system of this type is presented, based on a certain DSP board, but with other units and tasks easily inserted. A sample application in speech coding that utilizes these features is shown: a 14.5 kb/s real-time speech codec.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coding of colour picture using potential method
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A powerful system for the coding of colour pictures using the potential method is described. Decomposition of the chrominance vector is performed to match the colour features. Helmholtz's theorem is shown to be suitable for this purpose, and the vector field is decomposed into lamellar and vector components. In addition, a novel edge-detection scheme is proposed which uses flow-potential concepts.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Heterostructure FETs for high speed applications
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Summary form only given. The optimization of heterostructure FET (HFET) structures for digital applications is described. By trading some of the 2-D electron-gas density for better pinch-off characteristics, HFETs with high current driving capability and low subthreshold voltage leakage current can be achieved with an optimized single-quantum-well channel structure. In addition, an HFET structure and a self-aligned ion implantation process designed for fabricating both E-FETs and D-FETs at the same time are proposed. Excellent threshold voltage uniformity on a wafer and good reproducibility from wafer to wafer, which meet the requirements of LSI circuits, are expected.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive normalized lattice algorithm for LS FIR multichannel filters with linear phase
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel adaptive normalized lattice algorithm for the least-squares (LS) design of multichannel FIR (finite-impulse response) filters with symmetric impulse response is presented. A byproduct is an algorithm for the LS estimation of the unit step backward predictor, based on the simultaneous minimization of the forward and backward total squared error powers, which has successfully been used in MEM spectral analysis. An order-recursive scheme that computes the filters from the normalized lattice variables is also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Envelope and instantaneous phase considerations in speech modelling
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a low-bit-rate coding system where the envelope and instantaneous phase of the residual are used. A time-varying filter (short-delay filter) is excited by a signal composed by a parametric version of the residual, multiplied by a sequence from a codebook. Two alternatives are studied for the design of the codebook: sequences formed by random pulses and sequences formed by random phases to simulate the instantaneous phase of the residual.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault modeling for physical failures for CMOS circuits
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors propose a fault simulation model for CMOS VLSI circuits which can handle physical faults as gate-to-drain/source shorts. A relation is established between the inverse voltage of a fault-free inverter and the faulty output voltage of a faulty inverter. This relation is then used to study the propagation of the faulty signal through a successive gate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Programmable digital filter for high speed applications
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors describe a flexible approach to high-speed digital FIR (finite impulse response) filters which are electrically programmable by users. The internal system structure and the strategies chosen to minimize complexity and maximize speed are explained in some detail. The proposed filter has been realized in a 1.5- mu m HCMOS process. It is noted that, although the proposed filter has many applications in the general domain of real-time digital signal processing, it is of specific interest in the domain of video signal processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multivariable model-reference adaptive control
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An algorithm is presented for a discrete model-reference adaptive controller for a system, in which the number of inputs is equal to the number of outputs. This controller, an extension of a single-input scheme due to R. Lozano and Y.D. Landau (1981), provides correct tracking of reference model outputs by plant outputs, together with freedom of choice of output error transient response. The use of the algorithm is demonstrated for the demanding instance of decoupling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Near-optimal broadcasting figures in computer networks
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors develop an efficient algorithm (NOBF) to calculate a near-optimal broadcasting figure (a broadcast with a near-optimal transmission delay) in arbitrary point-to-point computer networks. This algorithm is based on the following heuristic: choose in each broadcast cycle those nodes that, on the one hand, are minimally linked to the nodes already informed and, on the other hand, maximize a certain function of weight. Static and dynamic assignments of weights have been considered. The efficiency of the algorithm is analyzed as a function of the transmission delay and the algorithmic complexity. Of all the functions of weight considered, the function based on the concept of accumulative depth stands out for its efficiency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FIR filters suitable for high rate processing using general purpose 16-bit mu Ps
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A simple window method for the design of FIR filters is proposed which involves the adjustment of the Kaiser window. It achieves wideband filtering when conventional 16-bit microprocessors are used for the implementation. This is possible because of the simple relationship established among most of the filter coefficients.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reduction methods of capacitor mismatch errors in switched-capacitor A/D, D/A converters
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Two kinds of methods have been proposed to compensate or eliminate the capacitor mismatch of switched-capacitor A/D (analog-to-digital) and D/A converters. In the first method, a cyclic D/A converter with the facility of the automatic compensation of the capacitor mismatch can be realized. In the second method, a ratio-independent cyclic A/D converter can be realized. Cyclic A/D and D/A converters designed using these methods are presented. Measurements on the proposed circuits built with discrete components proved the expected performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Large deviation exits from a running orbit in the Josephson junction
publicationTitle: 1988., IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A generalization of large deviation results to the instance where the diffusion matrix is singular is used to solve the problem of exit from the region of attraction of a stable limit cycle (running orbit) in the DC-forced Josephson junction. The associated variational problem is posed and solved as an optimal control problem. It is found that the likely exit path is through the saddle equilibrium on the separatrix. This path is computed and the asymptotic exit time is calculated. The problem of relative stability of the running orbit and the stable equilibrium is thus solved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency demultiplication phase-locking of relaxation oscillations for BNRT
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The frequency demultiplication phase-locking phenomenon in a relaxation-oscillating circuit under periodic external excitation is explained with the mathematical theory of the diffeomorphism of a circle circumference. This approach is applied to a bidirectional negative-resistance transistor (BNRT). Phase-locking zones in the parameter plane are computed and agree with experimental results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
